**Montenegro**[[d]](#cite_note-16) is a country in [Southeast Europe](/wiki/Southeast_Europe "Southeast Europe"), on the [Balkan Peninsula](/wiki/Balkan_Peninsula "Balkan Peninsula").[[13]](#cite_note-17) Its 25 [municipalities](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Montenegro "Municipalities of Montenegro") have a total population of 633,158 people in an area of 13,883 km2 (5,360 sq mi). It is bordered by [Serbia](/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") to the northeast, [Bosnia and Herzegovina](/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina") to the northwest, [Kosovo](/wiki/Kosovo "Kosovo") to the east, [Albania](/wiki/Albania "Albania") to the southeast, and [Croatia](/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") to the west, and has a coastline along the [Adriatic Sea](/wiki/Adriatic_Sea "Adriatic Sea") to the southwest.[[14]](#cite_note-Encyclopaedia_Britannica-18) The capital and largest city is [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica "Podgorica"), while [Cetinje](/wiki/Cetinje "Cetinje") is the [Old Royal Capital](/wiki/Old_Royal_Capital_Cetinje "Old Royal Capital Cetinje") and cultural centre.[[15]](#cite_note-:2-19)

Before the arrival of the Slav peoples in the Balkans in the 6th and 7th centuries CE, the area now known as Montenegro was inhabited principally by people known as [Illyrians](/wiki/Illyrians "Illyrians").
During the [Early Medieval](/wiki/Early_Medieval "Early Medieval") period, three principalities were located on the territory of modern-day Montenegro: [Duklja](/wiki/Duklja "Duklja"), roughly corresponding to the southern half; [Travunia](/wiki/Travunia "Travunia"), the west; and [Rascia](/wiki/Principality_of_Serbia_(early_medieval) "Principality of Serbia (early medieval)") proper, the north.[[16]](#cite_note-Luscombe-20)[[17]](#cite_note-Sedlar-21)[[18]](#cite_note-22) The [Principality of Zeta](/wiki/Zeta_under_the_Bal%C5%A1i%C4%87i "Zeta under the Balšići") emerged in the 14th and 15th centuries. From the late 14th century to the late 18th century, large parts of southern Montenegro were ruled by the [Venetian Republic](/wiki/Venetian_Republic "Venetian Republic") and incorporated into [Venetian Albania](/wiki/Venetian_Albania "Venetian Albania").[[19]](#cite_note-:0-23) The name *Montenegro* was first used to refer to the country in the late 15th century. After falling under [Ottoman Empire](/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") rule, Montenegro gained semi-autonomy in 1696 under the rule of the [House of Petrović-Njegoš](/wiki/House_of_Petrovi%C4%87-Njego%C5%A1 "House of Petrović-Njegoš"), first as a [theocracy](/wiki/Prince-Bishopric_of_Montenegro "Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro") and later as a secular [principality](/wiki/Principality_of_Montenegro "Principality of Montenegro"). Montenegro's independence was recognised by the [Great Powers](/wiki/Great_Powers "Great Powers") at the [Congress of Berlin](/wiki/Congress_of_Berlin "Congress of Berlin") in 1878. In 1910, the country became a [kingdom](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Montenegro "Kingdom of Montenegro"). After [World War I](/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), the kingdom became part of [Yugoslavia](/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia"). Following the [breakup of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia"), the republics of [Serbia](/wiki/Republic_of_Serbia_(1992%E2%80%932006) "Republic of Serbia (1992–2006)") and [Montenegro](/wiki/Republic_of_Montenegro_(1992%E2%80%932006) "Republic of Montenegro (1992–2006)") together proclaimed a [federation](/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro "Serbia and Montenegro"). In June 2006 Montenegro declared its independence following a [referendum](/wiki/2006_Montenegrin_independence_referendum "2006 Montenegrin independence referendum").[[20]](#cite_note-:3-24)

Montenegro has an [upper-middle-income economy](/wiki/Economy_of_Montenegro "Economy of Montenegro"), mostly [service-based](/wiki/Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy "Tertiary sector of the economy"), and is in [late transition](/wiki/Transition_economy "Transition economy") to a [market economy](/wiki/Market_economy "Market economy").[[21]](#cite_note-The_Heritage_Foundation_2021-25) It is a member of the [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), [NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO"), the [World Trade Organization](/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization"), the [Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe](/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe"), the [Council of Europe](/wiki/Council_of_Europe "Council of Europe"), and the [Central European Free Trade Agreement](/wiki/Central_European_Free_Trade_Agreement "Central European Free Trade Agreement").[[22]](#cite_note-mvp.gov.me-26) Montenegro is also a founding member of the [Union for the Mediterranean](/wiki/Union_for_the_Mediterranean "Union for the Mediterranean"),[[23]](#cite_note-European_Western_Balkans_2020-27) and has been in the process of [joining the European Union](/wiki/Accession_of_Montenegro_to_the_European_Union "Accession of Montenegro to the European Union") since 2012.[[24]](#cite_note-European_Neighbourhood_Policy_And_Enlargement_Negotiations_-_European_Commission_2016-28)

Etymology
---------

Montenegro's ([/ˌmɒntɪˈniːɡroʊ, -ˈneɪɡroʊ, -ˈnɛɡroʊ/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:En-us-Montenegro.ogg "File:En-us-Montenegro.ogg") [*MON-tin-E(E)G-roh, -⁠AY-groh*](/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key");[[25]](#cite_note-:4-29) [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language"): *Crna Gora*[[e]](#cite_note-native_name_2-30) / Црна Гора;[[f]](#cite_note-native_name_3-31) [Albanian](/wiki/Albanian_language "Albanian language"): *Mali i Zi*)[[26]](#cite_note-Vlada_Crne_Gore-32)[[27]](#cite_note-Влада_Црне_Горе-33) English name derives from a [Venetian](/wiki/Venetian_language "Venetian language") [calque](/wiki/Calque "Calque") of the [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language") phrase "*Crna Gora*", meaning literally "Black Mountain", deriving from the appearance of [Mount Lovćen](/wiki/Mount_Lov%C4%87en "Mount Lovćen"), which was covered in dense evergreen forests.[[28]](#cite_note-visit-montenegro-34) *Crna Gora* was mentioned for the first time in [edicts](/wiki/Edict "Edict") issued by [Stefan Uroš I](/wiki/Stefan_Uro%C5%A1_I "Stefan Uroš I") to the [Serbian Orthodox](/wiki/Serbian_Orthodox "Serbian Orthodox") [Zeta](/wiki/Zeta_(crown_land) "Zeta (crown land)") [Episcopate](/wiki/Episcopate "Episcopate") seat at [Vranjina island](/wiki/Vranjina_island "Vranjina island") in [Lake Skadar](/wiki/Lake_Skadar "Lake Skadar").[[29]](#cite_note-35) It came to denote the majority of contemporary Montenegro in the 15th century.[[30]](#cite_note-Fine532-36)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Map_Byzantine_Empire_1045_2000px_svg.png/250px-Map_Byzantine_Empire_1045_2000px_svg.png)](/wiki/File:Map_Byzantine_Empire_1045_2000px_svg.png)

Duklja in the 11th century

Modern-day Montenegro was more and more known by that name in the historical period following the fall of the [Serbian Despotate](/wiki/Serbian_Despotate "Serbian Despotate") in 1459.[[31]](#cite_note-37) Originally, it had referred to only a small strip of land under the rule of the [Paštrovići](/wiki/Pa%C5%A1trovi%C4%87i "Paštrovići") tribe, but the name eventually came to be used for the wider mountainous region after the [Crnojević noble family](/wiki/Crnojevi%C4%87_noble_family "Crnojević noble family") took power in [Upper Zeta](/wiki/Upper_Zeta "Upper Zeta").[[30]](#cite_note-Fine532-36) The aforementioned region became known as *Stara Crna Gora* '[Old Montenegro](/wiki/Old_Montenegro "Old Montenegro")' by the 19th century to distinguish the independent region from the neighbouring Ottoman-occupied Montenegrin territory of *Brda* (the "Highlands"). Montenegro further increased its size several times by the 20th century, as the result of wars against the [Ottoman Empire](/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire"), which saw the annexation of [Old Herzegovina](/wiki/Old_Herzegovina "Old Herzegovina") and parts of [Metohija](/wiki/Metohija "Metohija") and southern [Raška](/wiki/Ra%C5%A1ka_(region) "Raška (region)"). Its borders have changed little since then, losing Metohija and gaining the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor").[[32]](#cite_note-38)

After the second session of the [AVNOJ](/wiki/AVNOJ "AVNOJ") during [World War II in Yugoslavia](/wiki/World_War_II_in_Yugoslavia "World War II in Yugoslavia"), the contemporary modern state of Montenegro was founded as the *Federal State of Montenegro* ([Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language"): Савезна држава Црне Горе / *Savezna država Crne Gore*) on 15 November 1943 within the Yugoslav Federation by the [ZAVNOCGB](/wiki/ZAVNOCGB "ZAVNOCGB"). After the war, Montenegro became a republic under its name, the [People's Republic of Montenegro](/wiki/People%27s_Republic_of_Montenegro "People's Republic of Montenegro") ([Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language"): Народна Република Црна Гора / *Narodna Republika Crna Gora*) on 29 November 1945. In 1963, it was renamed to the [Socialist Republic of Montenegro](/wiki/Socialist_Republic_of_Montenegro "Socialist Republic of Montenegro") ([Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language"): Социјалистичка Република Црна Гора / *Socijalistička Republika Crna Gora*). As the [breakup of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia") occurred, the SRCG was renamed to the Republic of Montenegro ([Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language"): Република Црна Гора / *Republika Crna Gora*) on 27 April 1992 within the [Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") by removing the adjective "socialist" from the republic's title. Since 22 October 2007, a year after its independence, the name of the country became simply known as Montenegro. The country is known as *Mali i Zi* (lit. black mountain) in [Albanian](/wiki/Albanian_language "Albanian language"),[[33]](#cite_note-39) while it is known as *Crna Gora* in Montenegrin, Serbian, [Bosnian](/wiki/Bosniak_language "Bosniak language"), and [Croatian](/wiki/Croatian_language "Croatian language").

History
-------

Main article: [History of Montenegro](/wiki/History_of_Montenegro "History of Montenegro")

### Antiquity

Main articles: [Illyria](/wiki/Illyria "Illyria"), [Illyricum (Roman province)](/wiki/Illyricum_(Roman_province) "Illyricum (Roman province)"), [Dalmatia (Roman province)](/wiki/Dalmatia_(Roman_province) "Dalmatia (Roman province)"), and [Praevalitana](/wiki/Praevalitana "Praevalitana")

Modern-day Montenegro was part of [Illyria](/wiki/Illyria "Illyria") and populated by the Indo-European-speaking [Illyrians](/wiki/Illyrians "Illyrians").[[34]](#cite_note-Boardman629-40)[[35]](#cite_note-41)[[36]](#cite_note-42) The [Illyrian kingdom](/wiki/Illyrian_kingdom "Illyrian kingdom") was conquered by the [Roman Republic](/wiki/Roman_Republic "Roman Republic") in the [Illyro-Roman Wars](/wiki/Illyro-Roman_Wars "Illyro-Roman Wars") and the region was incorporated into the [province of Illyricum](/wiki/Illyricum_(Roman_province) "Illyricum (Roman province)") (later [Dalmatia](/wiki/Dalmatia_(Roman_province) "Dalmatia (Roman province)") and [Praevalitana](/wiki/Praevalitana "Praevalitana")).[[37]](#cite_note-43)[[38]](#cite_note-44)[[39]](#cite_note-45)

### Arrival of the Slavs

Main articles: [Duklja](/wiki/Duklja "Duklja"), [Principality of Zeta](/wiki/Principality_of_Zeta "Principality of Zeta"), and [Tribes of Montenegro](/wiki/Tribes_of_Montenegro "Tribes of Montenegro")

Three principalities were located on the territory: [Duklja](/wiki/Duklja "Duklja"), roughly corresponding to the southern half, [Travunia](/wiki/Travunia "Travunia"), the west, and [Raška](/wiki/Principality_of_Serbia_(early_medieval) "Principality of Serbia (early medieval)"), the north.[[16]](#cite_note-Luscombe-20)[[17]](#cite_note-Sedlar-21) Duklja gained its independence from the Byzantine Roman Empire in 1042.[[40]](#cite_note-46)[[41]](#cite_note-47) Over the next few decades, it expanded its territory to neighbouring Rascia and Bosnia, and also became recognised as a kingdom. Its power started declining at the beginning of the 12th century. After King Bodin's death (in 1101 or 1108), civil wars ensued. Duklja reached its zenith under Vojislav's son, [Mihailo](/wiki/Mihailo_I_of_Duklja "Mihailo I of Duklja") (1046–1081), and his grandson [Constantine Bodin](/wiki/Constantine_Bodin "Constantine Bodin") (1081–1101).[[42]](#cite_note-48)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Cytadela_w_obr%C4%99bie_mur%C3%B3w_miejskich_w_Kotorze_02.jpg/250px-Cytadela_w_obr%C4%99bie_mur%C3%B3w_miejskich_w_Kotorze_02.jpg)](/wiki/File:Cytadela_w_obr%C4%99bie_mur%C3%B3w_miejskich_w_Kotorze_02.jpg)

[Fortifications of Kotor](/wiki/Fortifications_of_Kotor "Fortifications of Kotor"). Built between the 9th and 19th centuries, [UNESCO World Heritage Site](/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site "UNESCO World Heritage Site").

As the nobility fought for the throne, the kingdom was weakened, and by 1186, the territory of modern-day Montenegro became part of the state ruled by [Stefan Nemanja](/wiki/Stefan_Nemanja "Stefan Nemanja") and was a part of various state formations ruled by the [Nemanjić dynasty](/wiki/Nemanji%C4%87_dynasty "Nemanjić dynasty") for the next two centuries. After the [Serbian Empire](/wiki/Serbian_Empire "Serbian Empire") collapsed in the second half of the 14th century, the most powerful Zetan family, the [Balšićs](/wiki/Bal%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Balšić"), became sovereigns of Zeta.[[43]](#cite_note-49)

By the 13th century, *Zeta* had replaced *Duklja* when referring to the realm.[[44]](#cite_note-50) In the late 14th century, southern Montenegro ([Zeta](/wiki/Lordship_of_Zeta "Lordship of Zeta")) came under the rule of the [Balšić noble family](/wiki/Bal%C5%A1i%C4%87_noble_family "Balšić noble family"), then the [Crnojević noble family](/wiki/Crnojevi%C4%87_noble_family "Crnojević noble family"), and by the 15th century, Zeta was more often referred to as *Crna Gora*.[[45]](#cite_note-51)

In 1421, Zeta was annexed to the [Serbian Despotate](/wiki/Serbian_Despotate "Serbian Despotate"), but after 1455, another noble family from Zeta, the [Crnojevićs](/wiki/Crnojevi%C4%87 "Crnojević"), became sovereign rulers of the country, making it the last free monarchy of the Balkans before it fell to the [Ottomans](/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") in 1496, and got annexed to the *[sanjak](/wiki/Sanjak "Sanjak")* of [Shkodër](/wiki/Shkod%C3%ABr "Shkodër"). For a short time, Montenegro existed as a separate autonomous *sanjak* in 1514–1528 ([Sanjak of Montenegro](/wiki/Sanjak_of_Montenegro "Sanjak of Montenegro")). Also, [Old Herzegovina](/wiki/Old_Herzegovina "Old Herzegovina") region was part of [Sanjak of Herzegovina](/wiki/Sanjak_of_Herzegovina "Sanjak of Herzegovina").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

### Early modern period

Main articles: [Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro](/wiki/Prince-Bishopric_of_Montenegro "Prince-Bishopric of Montenegro") and [Venetian Albania](/wiki/Venetian_Albania "Venetian Albania")

From 1392, numerous parts of the territory were controlled by [Republic of Venice](/wiki/Republic_of_Venice "Republic of Venice"), including the city of [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva"), in that time known as "Budua".
The Venetian territory was centred on the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor"), and the Republic introduced governors who meddled in Montenegrin politics.[[46]](#cite_note-52) Venice controlled territories in present-day Montenegro until [its fall](/wiki/Fall_of_the_Republic_of_Venice "Fall of the Republic of Venice") in 1797.[[19]](#cite_note-:0-23)[[47]](#cite_note-53)[[48]](#cite_note-54)
Large portions fell under the control of the [Ottoman Empire](/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") from 1496 to 1878. In the 16th century, Montenegro developed a unique form of autonomy within the Ottoman Empire that permitted Montenegrin clans freedom from certain restrictions. Nevertheless, the Montenegrins were disgruntled with Ottoman rule, and in the 17th century, repeatedly rebelled, which culminated in the defeat of the Ottomans in the [Great Turkish War](/wiki/Great_Turkish_War "Great Turkish War") at the end of that century.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/Petar_II_Petrovic-2.JPG/250px-Petar_II_Petrovic-2.JPG)](/wiki/File:Petar_II_Petrovic-2.JPG)

**Left:** [Petar I Petrović-Njegoš](/wiki/Petar_I_Petrovi%C4%87-Njego%C5%A1 "Petar I Petrović-Njegoš") was the most popular spiritual and military leader from the [Petrović dynasty](/wiki/Petrovi%C4%87_dynasty "Petrović dynasty").   
**Right:** [Petar II Petrović-Njegoš](/wiki/Petar_II_Petrovi%C4%87-Njego%C5%A1 "Petar II Petrović-Njegoš") was a [Prince-Bishop](/wiki/List_of_rulers_of_Montenegro "List of rulers of Montenegro") (*vladika*) of Montenegro and the national poet and philosopher. Oil painting of Njegoš as *vladika*, c. 1837

Montenegrin territories were controlled by warlike clans. Most clans had a chieftain (*knez*), who was not permitted to assume the title unless he proved to be as worthy a leader as his predecessor. An assembly of Montenegrin clans (*Zbor*) was held every year on 12 July in Cetinje, and any adult clansman could take part.[[49]](#cite_note-Visit_Montenegro-55) In 1515, Montenegro became a [theocracy](/wiki/Theocracy "Theocracy") led by the [Metropolitanate of Montenegro and the Littoral](/wiki/Metropolitanate_of_Montenegro_and_the_Littoral "Metropolitanate of Montenegro and the Littoral"), which flourished after the [Petrović-Njegoš](/wiki/Petrovi%C4%87-Njego%C5%A1 "Petrović-Njegoš") of Cetinje became the prince-bishop (whose title was "Vladika of Montenegro").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

People from Montenegro in this historical period were described as Orthodox Serbs.[[50]](#cite_note-56)

### Principality and Kingdom of Montenegro

Main articles: [Principality of Montenegro](/wiki/Principality_of_Montenegro "Principality of Montenegro") and [Kingdom of Montenegro](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Montenegro "Kingdom of Montenegro")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5d/Crna_Gora_-_Oslobodjenje_od_strane_okupacije_1711-1918.png/250px-Crna_Gora_-_Oslobodjenje_od_strane_okupacije_1711-1918.png)](/wiki/File:Crna_Gora_-_Oslobodjenje_od_strane_okupacije_1711-1918.png)

Expansion of Montenegro from 1711 to 1918 within present borders

In 1858, one of the major Montenegrin victories over the Ottomans occurred at the [Battle of Grahovac](/wiki/Battle_of_Grahovac "Battle of Grahovac"). [Grand Duke Mirko Petrović](/wiki/Mirko_Petrovi%C4%87_Njego%C5%A1 "Mirko Petrović Njegoš"), elder brother of [Knjaz Danilo](/wiki/Knjaz_Danilo "Knjaz Danilo"), led an army of 7,500 and defeated the numerically superior Ottomans with 15,000 troops at [Grahovac](/wiki/Grahovac,_Montenegro "Grahovac, Montenegro") on 1 May 1858. This forced the [Great Powers](/wiki/Great_Powers "Great Powers") to officially demarcate the borders between Montenegro and Ottoman Empire, *de facto* recognising Montenegro's independence.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In the [Battle of Vučji Do](/wiki/Battle_of_Vu%C4%8Dji_Do "Battle of Vučji Do") Montenegrins inflicted a major defeat on the Ottoman Army under Grand Vizier [Ahmed Muhtar Pasha](/wiki/Ahmed_Muhtar_Pasha "Ahmed Muhtar Pasha"). In the aftermath of the Russian victory against the Ottoman Empire in the [Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878](/wiki/Russo-Turkish_War_of_1877%E2%80%931878 "Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878"), the [major powers](/wiki/Great_powers_of_Europe "Great powers of Europe") restructured the map of the Balkan region. The Ottoman Empire recognised the independence of Montenegro in the [Treaty of Berlin](/wiki/Treaty_of_Berlin_(1878) "Treaty of Berlin (1878)") in 1878.[[51]](#cite_note-57)

The first Montenegrin constitution (also known as the Danilo Code) was proclaimed in 1855. Under [Nicholas I](/wiki/Nicholas_I_of_Montenegro "Nicholas I of Montenegro") (ruled 1860–1918), the [principality](/wiki/Principality "Principality") was enlarged several times in the Montenegro-Turkish Wars and was recognised as independent in 1878. Nicholas I established diplomatic relations with the Ottoman Empire.[[52]](#cite_note-58) Minor border skirmishes excepted, diplomacy ushered in about 30 years of peace between the two states until the deposition of [Abdul Hamid II](/wiki/Abdul_Hamid_II "Abdul Hamid II") in 1909.[[53]](#cite_note-ttk.gov.tr-59)

The political skills of Abdul Hamid II and Nicholas I played a major role in the mutually amicable relations.[[53]](#cite_note-ttk.gov.tr-59) Modernization of the state followed, culminating with the draft of a Constitution in 1905. However, political rifts emerged between the reigning [People's Party](/wiki/People%27s_Party_(Montenegro,_1906) "People's Party (Montenegro, 1906)"), who supported the process of democratisation and union with Serbia, and those of the [True People's Party](/wiki/True_People%27s_Party "True People's Party"), who were monarchist.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

In 1910, Montenegro became [a kingdom](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Montenegro "Kingdom of Montenegro"), and as a result of the [Balkan Wars](/wiki/Balkan_Wars "Balkan Wars") of 1912–1913, a common border with Serbia was established, with [Shkodër](/wiki/Shkod%C3%ABr "Shkodër") being awarded to [Albania](/wiki/Albania "Albania"), though the current capital city of Montenegro, Podgorica, was on the old border of Albania and Yugoslavia. Montenegro became one of the [Allied Powers](/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_I "Allies of World War I") during World War I (1914–1918). In the [Battle of Mojkovac](/wiki/Battle_of_Mojkovac "Battle of Mojkovac") fought in January 1916 between [Austria-Hungary](/wiki/Austria-Hungary "Austria-Hungary") and the Kingdom of Montenegro, Montenegrins achieved a decisive victory even though they were outnumbered five to one. The Austro-Hungarians accepted military surrender on 25 January 1916.[[54]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPopeWhealRobbins2003431-60) From 1916 to October 1918 Austria-Hungary occupied Montenegro. During the occupation, King Nicholas fled the country and established a [government-in-exile](/wiki/Government-in-exile "Government-in-exile") in [Bordeaux](/wiki/Bordeaux "Bordeaux").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

### Kingdom of Yugoslavia

Main article: [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia "Kingdom of Yugoslavia")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Locator_map_Zeta_Banovina_in_Yugoslavia_1929-1939.svg/250px-Locator_map_Zeta_Banovina_in_Yugoslavia_1929-1939.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Locator_map_Zeta_Banovina_in_Yugoslavia_1929-1939.svg)

Locator map of [Zeta Banovina](/wiki/Zeta_Banovina "Zeta Banovina") in [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia "Kingdom of Yugoslavia")

In 1922, Montenegro formally became the [Oblast of Cetinje](/wiki/Zeta_Oblast "Zeta Oblast") in the [Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Serbs,_Croats_and_Slovenes "Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes"), with the addition of the coastal areas around [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor"). In a further restructuring in 1929, it became a part of a larger [Zeta Banate](/wiki/Zeta_Banate "Zeta Banate") of the [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia "Kingdom of Yugoslavia") that reached the [Neretva](/wiki/Neretva "Neretva") River.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Nicholas's grandson, the Serb King [Alexander I](/wiki/Alexander_I_of_Yugoslavia "Alexander I of Yugoslavia"), dominated the Yugoslav government. [Zeta Banovina](/wiki/Zeta_Banovina "Zeta Banovina") was one of nine banovinas that formed the kingdom; it consisted of the present-day Montenegro and parts of Serbia, Croatia, and Bosnia.[[55]](#cite_note-61)

### World War II and Socialist Yugoslavia

Main articles: [Italian governorate of Montenegro](/wiki/Italian_governorate_of_Montenegro "Italian governorate of Montenegro") and [Socialist Republic of Montenegro](/wiki/Socialist_Republic_of_Montenegro "Socialist Republic of Montenegro")

In April 1941, [Nazi Germany](/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany"), the [Kingdom of Italy](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy"), and other Axis allies attacked and occupied the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. Italian forces occupied Montenegro and established a puppet [Kingdom of Montenegro](/wiki/Italian_governorate_of_Montenegro "Italian governorate of Montenegro").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/Osnivanje_Osme_crnogorske_brigade.jpg/250px-Osnivanje_Osme_crnogorske_brigade.jpg)](/wiki/File:Osnivanje_Osme_crnogorske_brigade.jpg)

Great People's Assembly on the occasion of the establishment of the Eighth Montenegrin Brigade in [Berane](/wiki/Berane "Berane"), 25 February 1944

In May, the Montenegrin branch of the Communist Party of Yugoslavia started preparations for an uprising planned for mid-July. The Communist Party and its Youth League organised 6,000 of its members into detachments prepared for [guerrilla warfare](/wiki/Guerrilla_warfare "Guerrilla warfare"). According to some historians, the first armed uprising in [Nazi](/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany")-occupied Europe happened on 13 July 1941 in Montenegro.[[56]](#cite_note-62)

Unexpectedly, the uprising took hold, and by 20 July, 32,000 men and women had joined the fight. Except for the coast and major towns (Podgorica, Cetinje, Pljevlja, and Nikšić), which were besieged, Montenegro was mostly liberated. In a month of fighting, the Italian army suffered 5,000 dead, wounded, and captured. The uprising lasted until mid-August, when it was suppressed by a counter-offensive of 67,000 Italian troops brought in from Albania. Faced with new and overwhelming Italian forces, many of the fighters laid down their arms and returned home. Nevertheless, intense guerrilla fighting lasted until December.

Fighters who remained under arms fractured into two groups. Most of them went on to join the Yugoslav Partisans, consisting of communists and those inclined towards active resistance; these included [Arso Jovanović](/wiki/Arso_Jovanovi%C4%87 "Arso Jovanović"), [Sava Kovačević](/wiki/Sava_Kova%C4%8Devi%C4%87 "Sava Kovačević"), [Svetozar Vukmanović-Tempo](/wiki/Svetozar_Vukmanovi%C4%87-Tempo "Svetozar Vukmanović-Tempo"), [Milovan Đilas](/wiki/Milovan_%C4%90ilas "Milovan Đilas"), [Peko Dapčević](/wiki/Peko_Dap%C4%8Devi%C4%87 "Peko Dapčević"), [Vlado Dapčević](/wiki/Vlado_Dap%C4%8Devi%C4%87 "Vlado Dapčević"), [Veljko Vlahović](/wiki/Veljko_Vlahovi%C4%87 "Veljko Vlahović"), and [Blažo Jovanović](/wiki/Bla%C5%BEo_Jovanovi%C4%87 "Blažo Jovanović"). Those loyal to the [Karađorđević dynasty](/wiki/Kara%C4%91or%C4%91evi%C4%87_dynasty "Karađorđević dynasty") and opposing communism went on to become [Chetniks](/wiki/Chetniks "Chetniks"), and turned to collaboration with Italians against the Partisans.

War broke out between Partisans and Chetniks during the first half of 1942. Pressured by Italians and Chetniks, the core of the Montenegrin Partisans went to Serbia and Bosnia, where they joined with other Yugoslav Partisans. Fighting between Partisans and Chetniks continued through the war. Chetniks with Italian backing controlled most of the country from mid-1942 to April 1943. Montenegrin Chetniks received the status of "anti-communist militia" and received weapons, ammunition, food rations, and money from Italy. Most of them were moved to [Mostar](/wiki/Mostar "Mostar"), where they fought in the [Battle of Neretva](/wiki/Battle_of_Neretva "Battle of Neretva") against the Partisans, but were dealt a heavy defeat.

During German operation Schwartz against the Partisans in May and June 1943, Germans disarmed many Chetniks without fighting, as they feared they would turn against them in case of an Allied invasion of the Balkans. After the capitulation of Italy in September 1943, Partisans managed to take hold of most of Montenegro for a brief time, but Montenegro was soon [occupied by German forces](/wiki/German_occupied_territory_of_Montenegro "German occupied territory of Montenegro"), and fierce fighting continued during late 1943 and 1944. Montenegro was liberated by the Partisans in December 1944.

Montenegro became one of the six constituent republics of the communist [Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") (SFRY). Its capital became Podgorica, renamed [Titograd](/wiki/Titograd "Titograd") in honour of President [Josip Broz Tito](/wiki/Josip_Broz_Tito "Josip Broz Tito"). After the war, the infrastructure of Yugoslavia was rebuilt, industrialization began, and the [University of Montenegro](/wiki/University_of_Montenegro "University of Montenegro") was established. Greater autonomy was established until the [Socialist Republic of Montenegro](/wiki/Socialist_Republic_of_Montenegro "Socialist Republic of Montenegro") ratified a new constitution in 1974.[[57]](#cite_note-Roberts_1978_pp._136–146-63)[[58]](#cite_note-64)

### Montenegro within FR Yugoslavia

Main articles: [Serbia and Montenegro](/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro "Serbia and Montenegro") and [Republic of Montenegro (1992–2006)](/wiki/Republic_of_Montenegro_(1992%E2%80%932006) "Republic of Montenegro (1992–2006)")

After the formal dissolution of the SFRY in 1992, Montenegro remained part of a smaller [Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") along with Serbia. In the [referendum on remaining in Yugoslavia in 1992](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_1992 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 1992"), 96% of the votes cast were in favour of the federation with Serbia. The referendum was boycotted by opposition parties such as the [Liberal Alliance of Montenegro](/wiki/Liberal_Alliance_of_Montenegro "Liberal Alliance of Montenegro"),[[59]](#cite_note-:1-65) the [Social Democratic](/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_of_Montenegro "Social Democratic Party of Montenegro") and Socialist Parties,[[60]](#cite_note-66) as well as minority parties such as the [Democratic League in Montenegro](/wiki/Democratic_League_in_Montenegro "Democratic League in Montenegro"),[[61]](#cite_note-67) leading to a relatively low turnout of 66%.[[59]](#cite_note-:1-65)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Former_Yugoslavia_durning_war.svg/500px-Former_Yugoslavia_durning_war.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Former_Yugoslavia_durning_war.svg)

Map of the [disintegration of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia") until 2008

During the 1991–1995 [Bosnian War](/wiki/Bosnian_War "Bosnian War") and [Croatian War](/wiki/Croatian_War "Croatian War"), Montenegrin police and military forces, under orders of president Momir Bulatovic[[62]](#cite_note-MD-68) and Interior Minister [Pavle Bulatovic](/wiki/Pavle_Bulatovic "Pavle Bulatovic")[[63]](#cite_note-69) joined Serbian troops in attacks on [Dubrovnik](/wiki/Dubrovnik "Dubrovnik"), Croatia.[[64]](#cite_note-70) These operations, aimed at acquiring more territory, were characterised by large-scale violations of human rights.[[65]](#cite_note-71)

Montenegrin General [Pavle Strugar](/wiki/Pavle_Strugar "Pavle Strugar") was convicted for his part in the bombing of Dubrovnik.[[66]](#cite_note-72) Bosnian refugees were arrested by Montenegrin police and transported to Serb camps in [Foča](/wiki/Fo%C4%8Da_ethnic_cleansing "Foča ethnic cleansing"), where they were subjected to systematic torture and executed.[[67]](#cite_note-73)

In 1996, [Milo Đukanović](/wiki/Milo_%C4%90ukanovi%C4%87 "Milo Đukanović")'s government severed ties between Montenegro and its partner Serbia, which was led by [Slobodan Milošević](/wiki/Slobodan_Milo%C5%A1evi%C4%87 "Slobodan Milošević"). Montenegro formed its own [economic policy](/wiki/Economic_policy "Economic policy") and adopted the German [Deutsche Mark](/wiki/Deutsche_Mark "Deutsche Mark") as its currency and subsequently [adopted the euro](/wiki/Montenegro_and_the_euro "Montenegro and the euro"), although not part of the [Eurozone](/wiki/Eurozone "Eurozone"). Subsequent governments pursued pro-independence policies, and political tensions with Serbia simmered despite political changes in [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade").

Targets in Montenegro were bombed by NATO forces during [Operation Allied Force](/wiki/Operation_Allied_Force "Operation Allied Force") in 1999, although the extent of these attacks was limited in both time and area affected.[[68]](#cite_note-74)

In 2002, Serbia and Montenegro came to a new agreement for continued cooperation and entered into negotiations regarding the future status of the [Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Federal Republic of Yugoslavia"). This resulted in the Belgrade Agreement, which saw the country's transformation into a more decentralised state union named [Serbia and Montenegro](/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro "Serbia and Montenegro") in 2003. The Belgrade Agreement also contained a provision delaying any future referendum on the independence of Montenegro for at least three years.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

### Independence

Main articles: [Serbia and Montenegro](/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro "Serbia and Montenegro") and [Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006")

See also: [2016 Montenegrin coup d'état attempt allegations](/wiki/2016_Montenegrin_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat_attempt_allegations "2016 Montenegrin coup d'état attempt allegations") and [2019–20 Montenegrin crisis](/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Montenegrin_crisis "2019–20 Montenegrin crisis")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Independent_montenegro.jpg/250px-Independent_montenegro.jpg)](/wiki/File:Independent_montenegro.jpg)

Supporters of Montenegrin independence in June 2006 in [Cetinje](/wiki/Cetinje "Cetinje")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Under_Secretary_Shannon_Poses_for_a_Photo_With_Montenegro%27s_Prime_Minister_Markovic%2C_Montenegro%27s_Foreign_Minister_Darmanovic%2C_and_NATO_Secretary-General_Stoltenberg_at_a_Ceremony_in_Washington_%2834734796140%29.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg)](/wiki/File:Under_Secretary_Shannon_Poses_for_a_Photo_With_Montenegro%27s_Prime_Minister_Markovic,_Montenegro%27s_Foreign_Minister_Darmanovic,_and_NATO_Secretary-General_Stoltenberg_at_a_Ceremony_in_Washington_(34734796140).jpg)

Montenegro Foreign Minister Srdjan Darmanović presents a document to [US](/wiki/US "US") Undersecretary of State for Political Affairs [Thomas Shannon](/wiki/Thomas_A._Shannon_Jr. "Thomas A. Shannon Jr.") and Montenegro Prime Minister [Duško Marković](/wiki/Du%C5%A1ko_Markovi%C4%87 "Duško Marković") during a ceremony at the [State Department](/wiki/State_Department "State Department") to accept Montenegro's instrument of accession to the [North Atlantic Treaty Organization](/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization "North Atlantic Treaty Organization") ([NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO")), 5 June 2017.

The status of the union between Montenegro and Serbia was decided by a [referendum on Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006") on 21 May 2006. A total of 419,240 votes were cast, representing 86.5% of the electorate; 230,661 votes (55.5%) were for independence and 185,002 votes (44.5%) were against.[[69]](#cite_note-75) This narrowly surpassed the 55% threshold needed to validate the referendum under the rules set by the European Union. According to the electoral commission, the 55% threshold was passed by only 2,300 votes. Serbia, the member-states of the European Union, and the [permanent members of the United Nations Security Council](/wiki/Permanent_members_of_the_United_Nations_Security_Council "Permanent members of the United Nations Security Council") all [recognised](/wiki/Diplomatic_recognition "Diplomatic recognition") Montenegro's independence.

The 2006 referendum was monitored by five international observer missions, headed by an [OSCE](/wiki/OSCE "OSCE")/[ODIHR](/wiki/ODIHR "ODIHR") team, and around 3,000 observers in total (including domestic observers from [CDT](/wiki/Center_for_Democracy_and_Technology "Center for Democracy and Technology") (OSCE PA), the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), the Congress of Local and Regional Authorities of the Council of Europe (CLRAE), and the European Parliament (EP) to form an International Referendum Observation Mission (IROM). The IROM—in its preliminary report—"assessed compliance of the referendum process with OSCE commitments, Council of Europe commitments, other international standards for democratic electoral processes, and domestic legislation." Furthermore, the report stated that the competitive pre-referendum environment was marked by an active and generally peaceful campaign and that "there were no reports of restrictions on fundamental civil and political rights".

On 3 June 2006, the Montenegrin Parliament declared the independence of Montenegro,[[70]](#cite_note-76) formally confirming the result of the referendum.

On 28 June 2006, Montenegro joined the [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") as its 192nd member state.[[71]](#cite_note-77)

Montenegro has been dominated since the breakup of Yugoslavia by [Milo Đukanović](/wiki/Milo_%C4%90ukanovi%C4%87 "Milo Đukanović") (four-time prime minister and twice president), accused of having established an [authoritarianism](/wiki/Authoritarianism "Authoritarianism") and [clientelist](/wiki/Clientelist "Clientelist") regime, while maintaining close relations with [organized crime](/wiki/Organized_crime "Organized crime").[[72]](#cite_note-78) The massive privatizations of the Đukanović era lead to the enrichment of him and oligarchs close to him. His brother Aleksandar, owner of Montenegro's first private bank, oversaw the privatizations, while his sister, Ana Kolarevic, has long controlled the judiciary. The clientelist networks of the ruling party dominated all segments of social life. A party card was required to start a business or obtain a position in the administration. This policy also contributed to the reinforcement of regional disparities and social inequalities. Unemployment climbs to 36.6 per cent in the northern part of the country, compared to 3.9 per cent in the coastal region, while a quarter of the population lives below the poverty line (2018).[[73]](#cite_note-79)

The [Law on the Status of the Descendants of the Petrović Njegoš Dynasty](/wiki/Law_on_the_Status_of_the_Descendants_of_the_Petrovi%C4%87_Njego%C5%A1_Dynasty "Law on the Status of the Descendants of the Petrović Njegoš Dynasty") was passed by the Parliament of Montenegro on 12 July 2011. It rehabilitated the [Royal House of Montenegro](/wiki/House_of_Petrovi%C4%87-Njego%C5%A1 "House of Petrović-Njegoš") and recognised limited symbolic roles within the constitutional framework of the republic.

In 2015, the investigative journalists' network [OCCRP](/wiki/OCCRP "OCCRP") named Montenegro's long-time President and Prime Minister [Milo Đukanović](/wiki/Milo_%C4%90ukanovi%C4%87 "Milo Đukanović") "Person of the Year in Organized Crime".[[74]](#cite_note-80) The extent of Đukanović's corruption led to street demonstrations and calls for his removal.[[75]](#cite_note-81)[[76]](#cite_note-82)

In October 2016, for the day of the [parliamentary election](/wiki/Montenegrin_parliamentary_election,_2016 "Montenegrin parliamentary election, 2016"), a [coup d'état was prepared](/wiki/Montenegrin_coup_d%27%C3%A9tat_attempt "Montenegrin coup d'état attempt") by a group of persons that included leaders of the Montenegrin opposition, Serbian nationals and Russian agents; the coup was prevented.[[77]](#cite_note-83) In 2017, fourteen people, including two Russian nationals and two Montenegrin opposition leaders, [Andrija Mandić](/wiki/Andrija_Mandi%C4%87 "Andrija Mandić") and [Milan Knežević](/wiki/Milan_Kne%C5%BEevi%C4%87_(Montenegrin_politician) "Milan Knežević (Montenegrin politician)"), were indicted for their alleged roles in the coup attempt on charges such as "preparing a conspiracy against the constitutional order and the security of Montenegro" and an "attempted terrorist act".[[78]](#cite_note-rferlcoup-84)

### Recent history

Montenegro formally [became a member](/wiki/Montenegro%E2%80%93NATO_relations "Montenegro–NATO relations") of [NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO") in June 2017, despite attempts by Russia to sabotage it,[[79]](#cite_note-murkypolitico-85) an event that triggered a promise of retaliatory actions from [Russia's government](/wiki/Government_of_Russia "Government of Russia").[[80]](#cite_note-86)[[81]](#cite_note-87)[[82]](#cite_note-88)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Protest_in_Kotor%2C_Jan_2020.jpg/250px-Protest_in_Kotor%2C_Jan_2020.jpg)](/wiki/File:Protest_in_Kotor,_Jan_2020.jpg)

The controversial 2019 [law on religious communities](/wiki/2019-2020_clerical_protests_in_Montenegro#Background "2019-2020 clerical protests in Montenegro"), introduced by the former ruling [DPS](/wiki/Democratic_Party_of_Socialists_of_Montenegro "Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro"), proposed the transfer of the majority of religious objects and land owned by the largest religious organization in the country, the [Serbian Orthodox Church](/wiki/Serbian_Orthodox_Church "Serbian Orthodox Church"), to the Montenegrin state. It sparked a [series of massive protests](/wiki/2019%E2%80%932020_clerical_protests_in_Montenegro "2019–2020 clerical protests in Montenegro"), which led to the first [government change](/wiki/2020_Montenegrin_parliamentary_election "2020 Montenegrin parliamentary election") in the country's history.

Montenegro has been in [negotiations](/wiki/Accession_of_Montenegro_to_the_European_Union "Accession of Montenegro to the European Union") with the EU since 2012.[[83]](#cite_note-89)[[84]](#cite_note-:5-90) In 2018, the earlier goal of acceding by 2022[[85]](#cite_note-91) was revised to 2025.[[86]](#cite_note-92) As of 2024, all 33 negotiation chapters had been opened, with three provisionally closed.[[87]](#cite_note-93)[[88]](#cite_note-94) Legislation is being passed bringing Montenegro law in line with EU membership requirements.[[84]](#cite_note-:5-90)

In April 2018, [Milo Djukanovic](/wiki/Milo_Djukanovic "Milo Djukanovic"), the leader of the ruling [Democratic Party of Socialists](/wiki/Democratic_Party_of_Socialists "Democratic Party of Socialists") (DPS), won Montenegro's [presidential election](/wiki/2018_Montenegrin_presidential_election "2018 Montenegrin presidential election"). The veteran politician had served as Prime Minister six times and as president once before. He had dominated Montenegrin politics since 1991.[[89]](#cite_note-95)

[Anti-corruption protests](/wiki/2019_Montenegrin_anti-corruption_protests "2019 Montenegrin anti-corruption protests") began in February 2019 against Đukanović and the Prime Minister [Duško Marković](/wiki/Du%C5%A1ko_Markovi%C4%87 "Duško Marković")-led [government](/wiki/Government_of_Montenegro#Marković_Cabinet_(2016-present) "Government of Montenegro") of the ruling [Democratic Party of Socialists](/wiki/Democratic_Party_of_Socialists "Democratic Party of Socialists") (DPS), which had been in power since 1991.[[90]](#cite_note-96)[[91]](#cite_note-97)

As of late December 2019,[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Montenegro&action=edit) the newly adopted Law on Religion, which [de jure](/wiki/De_jure "De jure") transferred the ownership of church buildings and estates built before 1918 from the [Serbian Orthodox Church](/wiki/Serbian_Orthodox_Church "Serbian Orthodox Church") to the Montenegrin state,[[92]](#cite_note-98)[[93]](#cite_note-99) sparked large[[94]](#cite_note-100) [protests](/wiki/2019%E2%80%932020_clerical_protests_in_Montenegro "2019–2020 clerical protests in Montenegro") and road blockages.[[95]](#cite_note-101)[[96]](#cite_note-102)[[97]](#cite_note-103) Seventeen opposition [Democratic Front](/wiki/Democratic_Front_(Montenegro) "Democratic Front (Montenegro)") MPs were arrested prior to the voting for disrupting the vote.[[98]](#cite_note-104) Demonstrations continued into March[[99]](#cite_note-105) 2020 as peaceful protest walks, mostly organised by the Serbian Orthodox Church in the majority of Montenegrin municipalities.[[100]](#cite_note-106)[[101]](#cite_note-107)[[102]](#cite_note-108)

In its political rights and civil liberties worldwide report in May 2020, [Freedom House](/wiki/Freedom_House "Freedom House") marked Montenegro as a [hybrid regime](/wiki/Hybrid_regime "Hybrid regime") rather than a democracy because of declining standards in governance, justice, elections, and media freedom.[[103]](#cite_note-109)[[104]](#cite_note-110) For the first time in three decades, in the [2020 parliamentary election](/wiki/2020_Montenegrin_parliamentary_election "2020 Montenegrin parliamentary election"), the opposition won more votes than Đukanović's ruling party.[[105]](#cite_note-111) In February 2022, that very same government was voted out in the first successful vote of no-confidence in the country's history.[[106]](#cite_note-112)

In September 2022, an investigation linked six Russian diplomats with twenty eight Russian citizens holding temporary visas for Montenegro and two local citizens in a spy investigation. The diplomats were expelled.[[107]](#cite_note-113) The Russian citizens were later banned from Montenegro and the two locals, one an ex-diplomat, face charges of illegal weapons, organising a criminal organisation and espionage.[[108]](#cite_note-114)

In March 2023, [Jakov Milatovic](/wiki/Jakov_Milatovic "Jakov Milatovic"), a pro-western candidate of the [Europe Now](/wiki/Europe_Now "Europe Now") movement, won the presidential [election](/wiki/2023_Montenegrin_presidential_election "2023 Montenegrin presidential election") run-off over incumbent Milo Djukanovic to succeed him as the incumbent [president of Montenegro](/wiki/President_of_Montenegro "President of Montenegro").[[109]](#cite_note-115) The [Europe Now](/wiki/Europe_Now "Europe Now") movement won the highest number of seats in the [2023 Montenegrin parliamentary election](/wiki/2023_Montenegrin_parliamentary_election "2023 Montenegrin parliamentary election").[[110]](#cite_note-116)[[111]](#cite_note-117) On 31 October 2023, [Milojko Spajic](/wiki/Milojko_Spajic "Milojko Spajic") of the Europe Now Movement became Montenegro's new prime minister, leading a coalition of both pro-European and pro-Serb parties.[[112]](#cite_note-118)

The [Parliament of Montenegro](/wiki/Parliament_of_Montenegro "Parliament of Montenegro") in June 2024 adopted a resolution acknowledging the atrocities committed at the [Jasenovac concentration camp](/wiki/Jasenovac_concentration_camp "Jasenovac concentration camp") during [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[113]](#cite_note-119) This decision, spearheaded by pro-Serbian factions, is viewed as a response to Montenegro's earlier support for a [UN](/wiki/UN "UN") resolution on the [Srebrenica genocide](/wiki/Srebrenica_genocide "Srebrenica genocide"). [Croatia](/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") has criticized the move, accusing Montenegro of politicizing historical events and warned that it could harm [Montenegro's path to EU membership](/wiki/Accession_of_Montenegro_to_the_European_Union "Accession of Montenegro to the European Union") and bilateral relations between [Croatia](/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") and Montenegro. The resolution has led to increased diplomatic tensions between the two nations.[[114]](#cite_note-120)

In 2024, Montenegro was one of 22 countries with a [Global Hunger Index](/wiki/Global_Hunger_Index "Global Hunger Index") score of less than 5.[[115]](#cite_note-121)

Geography
---------

Main article: [Geography of Montenegro](/wiki/Geography_of_Montenegro "Geography of Montenegro")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Montenegro_Map.png/330px-Montenegro_Map.png)](/wiki/File:Montenegro_Map.png)

Map of Montenegro

Montenegro features high peaks along its borders with Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, and Serbia. Its geography also includes a segment of the [karst](/wiki/Karst "Karst") of the western Balkan Peninsula, to a narrow coastal plain that is only 1.5 to 6 kilometres (1 to 4 miles) wide. The plain stops abruptly in the north, where [Mount Lovćen](/wiki/Mount_Lov%C4%87en "Mount Lovćen") and [Mount Orjen](/wiki/Mount_Orjen "Mount Orjen") plunge into the inlet of the Bay of Kotor.[[116]](#cite_note-The_Natural_Adventure_2023_x643-122)

Montenegro's large karst region lies generally at elevations of 1,000 metres (3,280 ft) above sea level; some parts, however, rise to 2,000 m (6,560 ft), such as [Mount Orjen](/wiki/Mount_Orjen "Mount Orjen") 1,894 metres (6,210 ft), the highest massif among the coastal limestone ranges. The [Zeta River](/wiki/Zeta_River "Zeta River") valley, at an elevation of 500 m (1,600 ft), is the lowest segment.

The mountains of Montenegro include some of the most rugged terrains in Europe, averaging more than 2,000 metres (6,600 feet) in elevation. One of the country's notable peaks is [Bobotov Kuk](/wiki/Bobotov_Kuk "Bobotov Kuk") in the [Durmitor](/wiki/Durmitor "Durmitor") mountains, which reaches a height of 2,522 metres (8,270 ft) and was previously thought to be the country's highest point. In 2018, new [triangulation](/wiki/Triangulation "Triangulation") measurements showed that [Zla Kolata](/wiki/Zla_Kolata "Zla Kolata") in the [Prokletije](/wiki/Prokletije "Prokletije") mountains, which reaches a height of 2,534 metres (8,310 ft).[[117]](#cite_note-Gajević_Gajević_2023_c815-123) Owing to the hyperhumid climate on their western sides, the Montenegrin mountain ranges were among the most ice-eroded parts of the Balkan Peninsula during the last glacial period.

Internationally, Montenegro borders [Serbia](/wiki/Serbia "Serbia"), [Bosnia and Herzegovina](/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"), [Kosovo](/wiki/Kosovo "Kosovo"), [Albania](/wiki/Albania "Albania") and [Croatia](/wiki/Croatia "Croatia"). It lies between latitudes [41°](/wiki/41st_parallel_north "41st parallel north") and [44°N](/wiki/44%C2%B0N "44°N"), and longitudes [18°](/wiki/18th_meridian_east "18th meridian east") and [21°E](/wiki/21st_meridian_east "21st meridian east").

Montenegro has many national parks, making it important for its biodiversity. The national parks include: the [Durmitor National Park](/wiki/Durmitor_National_Park "Durmitor National Park") (1952), having an area of 390 square kilometres (39,000 ha), is also a massif. Located in the [Dinaric Alps](/wiki/Dinaric_Alps "Dinaric Alps"), the Belgrade–Bar railway crosses the mountains in it; the [Biogradska Gora National Park](/wiki/Biogradska_Gora_National_Park "Biogradska Gora National Park") (1952), spans to 54 square kilometres (5,400 ha), being as well a forest, the park was recognised as one of the [UNESCO](/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") [World Network of Biosphere Reserves](/wiki/World_Network_of_Biosphere_Reserves "World Network of Biosphere Reserves"); the [Lovćen National Park](/wiki/Lov%C4%87en "Lovćen") (1952) is located in southwestern Montenegro, it is the inspiration behind the names of Montenegro and *[Crna Gora](/wiki/Crna_Gora "Crna Gora")*, the area is 64 square kilometres (6,400 ha); the [Lake Skadar National Park](/wiki/Lake_Skadar "Lake Skadar") (1983) is a big lake lying on the [Albania-Montenegro border](/wiki/Albania-Montenegro_border "Albania-Montenegro border"), the national park measure approximately 400 square kilometres (40,000 ha); the [Prokletije National Park](/wiki/Prokletije "Prokletije") (2009) is a mountain range including [the second tallest mountain of Montenegro](/wiki/Gjeravica "Gjeravica"), the park have an area of 166 square kilometres (16,600 ha).

Montenegro is a member of the [International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River](/wiki/International_Commission_for_the_Protection_of_the_Danube_River "International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River"), as more than 2,000 km2 (772 sq mi) of the country's territory lie within the [Danube](/wiki/Danube "Danube") [catchment area](/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin").

### Biodiversity

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/NP_Lov%C4%87en_%28by_Pudelek%29_01.jpg/250px-NP_Lov%C4%87en_%28by_Pudelek%29_01.jpg)](/wiki/File:NP_Lov%C4%87en_(by_Pudelek)_01.jpg)

[Lovćen](/wiki/Lov%C4%87en "Lovćen"), southern region of Montenegro

The diversity of the geological base, landscape, climate, and soil, and the position of Montenegro on the Balkan Peninsula and Adriatic Sea, created the conditions for high biological diversity, putting Montenegro among the "hot-spots" of European and world biodiversity. The number of species per area unit index in Montenegro is 0.837, the highest in any European country.[[118]](#cite_note-124)

Biological estimates suggest that over 1,200 species of freshwater algae, 300 species of marine algae, 589 species of moss, 7,000–8,000 species of vascular plants, 2,000 species of fungi, 16,000–20,000 species of insects, 407 species of marine fish, 56 species of reptile, 333 species of regularly visiting birds and a high species diversity of mammals are found in Montenegro.[[119]](#cite_note-Convention_on_Biological_Diversity_1970-125)

Montenegro can be divided into two main [biogeographic](/wiki/Biogeographic "Biogeographic") regions, which include the [Mediterranean Biogeographic Region](/wiki/Mediterranean_Biogeographic_Region "Mediterranean Biogeographic Region") and the [Alpine Biogeographic Region](/wiki/Alpine_Biogeographic_Region "Alpine Biogeographic Region").[[119]](#cite_note-Convention_on_Biological_Diversity_1970-125) It is also home to three terrestrial ecoregions: [Balkan mixed forests](/wiki/Balkan_mixed_forests "Balkan mixed forests"), [Dinaric Mountains mixed forests](/wiki/Dinaric_Mountains_mixed_forests "Dinaric Mountains mixed forests"), and [Illyrian deciduous forests](/wiki/Illyrian_deciduous_forests "Illyrian deciduous forests").[[120]](#cite_note-DinersteinOlson2017-126) It had a 2019 [Forest Landscape Integrity Index](/wiki/Forest_Landscape_Integrity_Index "Forest Landscape Integrity Index") mean score of 6.41/10, ranking it 73rd globally out of 172 countries.[[121]](#cite_note-FLII-Supplementary-127)

The total share of protected areas in Montenegro is 9.05% of the country's area, which mainly comes from the five [national parks of Montenegro](/wiki/National_parks_of_Montenegro "National parks of Montenegro").[[119]](#cite_note-Convention_on_Biological_Diversity_1970-125)

Politics
--------

Main article: [Politics of Montenegro](/wiki/Politics_of_Montenegro "Politics of Montenegro")

[![Jakov Milatović](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Jakov_Milatovi%C4%87_%282024-12-18%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Jakov_Milatovi%C4%87_%282024-12-18%29_%28cropped%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Jakov_Milatovi%C4%87_(2024-12-18)_(cropped).jpg)

Montenegro is a [parliamentary](/wiki/Parliamentary_system "Parliamentary system") [representative democratic](/wiki/Representative_democratic "Representative democratic") [republic](/wiki/Republic "Republic") with a [codified constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_Montenegro "Constitution of Montenegro") established in 2007. The constitution describes Montenegro as a "[civic](/wiki/Civic_engagement "Civic engagement"), democratic, [ecological](/wiki/Environmentalism "Environmentalism") state of [social justice](/wiki/Social_justice "Social justice"), based on the [reign of Law](/wiki/Rule_of_law "Rule of law")".[[122]](#cite_note-128) Montenegro is a [multi-party system](/wiki/Multi-party_system "Multi-party system").

The [President of Montenegro](/wiki/President_of_Montenegro "President of Montenegro") is the representative [head of state](/wiki/Head_of_state "Head of state"), elected for a period of five years through [direct election](/wiki/Direct_election "Direct election"). The President promotes the country internationally through diplomatic engagements, promulgates laws by ordinance, calls elections for the [Parliament](/wiki/Parliament_of_Montenegro "Parliament of Montenegro"), and ceremonially proposes candidates for [Prime Minister](/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Montenegro "Prime Minister of Montenegro"), president and justices of the Constitutional Court to the Parliament. The President also ceremonially proposes the calling of a [referendum](/wiki/Referendum "Referendum") to Parliament, grants amnesty for criminal offences proscribed by the national law, confers decoration and awards and performs other constitutional duties and is a member of the Supreme Defence Council. The official residence of the President is in [Cetinje](/wiki/Cetinje "Cetinje"). The incumbent president is [Jakov Milatović](/wiki/Jakov_Milatovi%C4%87 "Jakov Milatović") who has held the position since May 2023.

The [Government of Montenegro](/wiki/Government_of_Montenegro "Government of Montenegro") is the [executive branch](/wiki/Executive_branch "Executive branch") of government authority of Montenegro and led by the [Prime Minister](/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Montenegro "Prime Minister of Montenegro").[[123]](#cite_note-129) The role of Prime Minister is the most politically powerful office in Montenegro. All of Montenegro's governments since 2006 have been [coalitions](/wiki/Coalition_government "Coalition government") comprising a minimum of three [political parties.](/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Montenegro "List of political parties in Montenegro") The government is primarily based in [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica "Podgorica").

The [Parliament of Montenegro](/wiki/Parliament_of_Montenegro "Parliament of Montenegro") is the country's [unicameral](/wiki/Unicameral "Unicameral") [legislature](/wiki/Legislature "Legislature"), located in [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica "Podgorica"). The Parliament has power to appoint the government, pass [legislation](/wiki/Legislation "Legislation") (parliamentary law) and [scrutinise](/wiki/Legislative_scrutiny "Legislative scrutiny") [bills](/wiki/Bill_(law) "Bill (law)") (proposed parliamentary law). It also appoints justices of all courts, approves the budget and performs other duties as established by the country's Constitution. Parliament can pass a [motion of no confidence](/wiki/Motion_of_no_confidence "Motion of no confidence") in the Government by [simple majority vote](/wiki/Simple_majority_vote "Simple majority vote"). One member of the Montenegrin parliament, known as a Deputy, is elected per 6,000 voters.[[124]](#cite_note-130) There are currently 81 deputies. Elections to the Parliament are conducted by the [D'Hondt method](/wiki/D%27Hondt_method "D'Hondt method"), a form of [proportional representation](/wiki/Proportional_representation "Proportional representation").

According to [International IDEA](/wiki/International_Institute_for_Democracy_and_Electoral_Assistance "International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance")’s Global State of Democracy (GSoD) Indices and Democracy Tracker, Montenegro performs in the mid-range on overall democratic measures, with particular weaknesses in absence of corruption and judicial independence.[[125]](#cite_note-131)[[126]](#cite_note-132)[[127]](#cite_note-133) In 2019, Montenegro was described as a [hybrid regime](/wiki/Hybrid_regime "Hybrid regime") (a political system which combines [democratic](/wiki/Democracy "Democracy") and [authoritarian](/wiki/Authoritarian "Authoritarian") features) according to the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States")–based [Freedom House](/wiki/Freedom_House "Freedom House"). The organisation cited [state capture](/wiki/State_capture "State capture"), abuse of power, and strongman tactics by Prime Minister [Milo Đukanović](/wiki/Milo_%C4%90ukanovi%C4%87 "Milo Đukanović") (2008–2010 and 2012–2016) as explanations for its description as such. [Đukanović](/wiki/Milo_%C4%90ukanovi%C4%87 "Milo Đukanović") held a number of senior government positions, including the Presidency, before and after the dissolution of the union between Serbia and Montenegro. Similarly the *[Economist Democracy Index](/wiki/Economist_Democracy_Index "Economist Democracy Index")* (EDI) considers Montenegro to be a "flawed democracy": since it was first published, the EDI ranked Montenegro as a “flawed democracy” from 2006-2015, downgrading it to a “hybrid regime” between 2016-2020, before reinstating it to “flawed democracy in 2021 where, as of 2024, it remains.[[128]](#cite_note-134)[[129]](#cite_note-135)

[Đukanović](/wiki/Milo_%C4%90ukanovi%C4%87 "Milo Đukanović")'s [pro-European](/wiki/Pro-European "Pro-European") and [pro-NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO") [Democratic Party of Socialists](/wiki/Democratic_Party_of_Socialists "Democratic Party of Socialists") (DPS) narrowly lost the [2020 parliamentary election](/wiki/2020_Montenegrin_parliamentary_election "2020 Montenegrin parliamentary election") which ended the party's 30-year rule[[130]](#cite_note-136) and the pro-Serbia "[For the Future of Montenegro](/wiki/For_the_Future_of_Montenegro "For the Future of Montenegro")" (ZBCG) [parliamentary group](/wiki/Parliamentary_group "Parliamentary group"), composed mainly of Serb nationalist parties, formed a government under Prime Minister [Zdravko Krivokapic.](/wiki/Zdravko_Krivokapi%C4%87 "Zdravko Krivokapić")[[131]](#cite_note-137) Prime Minister Krivokapic's government was toppled in a no-confidence vote after just 14 months in power.[[132]](#cite_note-138)

In April 2022, a new [minority government](/wiki/Minority_government "Minority government"), led by Prime Minister [Dritan Abazović](/wiki/Dritan_Abazovi%C4%87 "Dritan Abazović"), brought together [moderate](/wiki/Moderate "Moderate") parties that are both pro-European and pro-Serb. However, his government lost a confidence vote after only 113 days. Since Montenegro had been unable to find a government which could command the confidence of the Parliament,[[133]](#cite_note-139) [Abazović](/wiki/Abazovi%C4%87 "Abazović") remained in his post until the [Spajić Cabinet](/wiki/Spaji%C4%87_Cabinet "Spajić Cabinet") had been formed after the [Parliamentary election which took place on 11 June 2023](/wiki/2023_Montenegrin_parliamentary_election "2023 Montenegrin parliamentary election"), where the [Europe Now!](/wiki/Europe_Now! "Europe Now!") party led by [Milojko Spajić](/wiki/Milojko_Spaji%C4%87 "Milojko Spajić") won the most seats.[[134]](#cite_note-140) In October 2023, a new minority government with [confidence and supply](/wiki/Confidence_and_supply "Confidence and supply") support from [ZBCG](/wiki/For_the_Future_of_Montenegro "For the Future of Montenegro") enabled [Milojko Spajić](/wiki/Milojko_Spaji%C4%87 "Milojko Spajić") to become the new prime minister.[[135]](#cite_note-141)
