255 | 3 | 20,265 | 4 |\\n\\n### Foreign relations\\n\\nSee also: [Foreign relations of Montenegro](/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Montenegro \"Foreign relations of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/NATO_Summit_2025_%2854611755854%29.jpg/250px-NATO_Summit_2025_%2854611755854%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:NATO_Summit_2025_(54611755854).jpg)\\n\\n[President of Montenegro](/wiki/President_of_Montenegro \"President of Montenegro\") [Jakov Milatović](/wiki/Jakov_Milatovi%C4%87 \"Jakov Milatović\") at the [North Atlantic Treaty Organization](/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty_Organization \"North Atlantic Treaty Organization\") Summit held in The Hague, Netherlands, on 24–25 June 2025. Montenegro became a member of [NATO](/wiki/NATO \"NATO\") 5 June 2017.\\n\\nThe Ministry of [Foreign Affairs](/wiki/Foreign_Affairs \"Foreign Affairs\") was given the task of defining the foreign policy priorities and activities needed for their implementation in cooperation with other state administration authorities, the President, the Speaker of the Parliament, and other relevant stakeholders.[[137]](#cite_note-mvpei.gov.me-143)\\n\\nThe country joined [NATO](/wiki/NATO \"NATO\") on 5 June 2017.[[138]](#cite_note-144) [Integration into the European Union](/wiki/Accession_of_Montenegro_to_the_European_Union \"Accession of Montenegro to the European Union\") remains a high-priority for Montenegro and has been the focus of Montenegrin foreign policy since its independence from Serbia.[[139]](#cite_note-145) In June 2023, newly elected President Milatović stated that he expects Montenegro to [join the European Union](/wiki/Accession_of_Montenegro_to_the_European_Union \"Accession of Montenegro to the European Union\") by 2027 or 2028.[[140]](#cite_note-146)\\n\\n### Law\\n\\nMain article: [Constitution of Montenegro](/wiki/Constitution_of_Montenegro \"Constitution of Montenegro\")\\n\\nThe current [Constitution of Montenegro](/wiki/Constitution_of_Montenegro \"Constitution of Montenegro\") was ratified and adopted by the [Constitutional Parliament](/wiki/Parliament_of_Montenegro \"Parliament of Montenegro\") of Montenegro on 19 October 2007 in a session by achieving the required two-thirds [supermajority](/wiki/Supermajority \"Supermajority\") of votes.[[141]](#cite_note-147)[[142]](#cite_note-148) It was officially proclaimed on 22 October 2007.[[143]](#cite_note-149)\\n\\nThe Constitution defines Montenegro as a civic, [democratic](/wiki/Democracy \"Democracy\") and [environmentally friendly](/wiki/Environmentally_friendly \"Environmentally friendly\") country with [social justice](/wiki/Social_justice \"Social justice\"), established by the [sovereign rights](/wiki/Sovereign_rights \"Sovereign rights\") of its government.[[144]](#cite_note-Pobjeda-150)[[145]](#cite_note-CafedelMontenegro-151)\\n\\nThe judiciary in Montenegro is composed of several courts, with the Supreme Court being the highest judicial authority. It oversees the uniform application of laws. Administrative Courts handle disputes related to public administration. The judiciary also includes Basic Courts (for minor civil and criminal cases), High Courts (for more serious cases and appeals), and the Appellate Court for reviewing lower court decisions.\\n\\nThe Constitutional Court is a separate body, tasked with safeguarding the constitution by reviewing laws and acts of public authorities to ensure their compliance with the Constitution.\\n\\nJudges in Montenegro are appointed by the Judicial Council and serve until the age of 67. The [President of Montenegro](/wiki/President_of_Montenegro \"President of Montenegro\") appoints judges upon the recommendation of the Judicial Council. Additionally, the Protector of Human Rights and Freedoms of Montenegro (Ombudsman) is appointed by the Parliament for a six-year term, ensuring the protection of human rights and social justice.\\n\\nDiscrimination on the basis of both [sexual orientation](/wiki/Sexual_orientation \"Sexual orientation\") and [gender identity](/wiki/Gender_identity \"Gender identity\") is banned in employment, the provision of goods and services, education and health services. Montenegro also possesses [hate crime](/wiki/Hate_crime \"Hate crime\") and [hate speech](/wiki/Hate_speech \"Hate speech\") laws which include sexual orientation and gender identity as grounds of non-discrimination.\\nSince 15 July 2021, same-sex couples may register their relationship as a [Life Partnership](/wiki/Recognition_of_same-sex_unions_in_Montenegro \"Recognition of same-sex unions in Montenegro\").\\n\\n### Law enforcement, security and emergency services\\n\\nMain article: [Police Directorate of Montenegro](/wiki/Police_Directorate_of_Montenegro \"Police Directorate of Montenegro\")\\n\\nLaw enforcement in Montenegro is carried out by several agencies under the [Ministry of Interior](/wiki/Ministry_of_Interior_(Montenegro) \"Ministry of Interior (Montenegro)\").\\nCivil law enforcement in Montenegro is primarily the responsibility of the Police Directorate, the national police force. [Municipal police](/wiki/Municipal_police \"Municipal police\"), known as Communal Police, enforce local laws in their respective municipalities.[[146]](#cite_note-152)\\n\\nLaw enforcement in Montenegro is carried out by several agencies under the [Ministry of Interior](/wiki/Ministry_of_Interior_(Montenegro) \"Ministry of Interior (Montenegro)\").\\nThe primary law enforcement body is the Montenegrin Police Directorate, responsible for crime investigation, maintaining public order, and general law enforcement. The Municipal Police assist with local law enforcement tasks, primarily focusing on traffic regulation and minor public order issues.[[147]](#cite_note-153)\\nPrivate security firms operate in Montenegro but have no legal authority to arrest or detain suspects.\\n\\nThe [National Security Agency (ANB)](/wiki/National_Security_Agency_(Montenegro) \"National Security Agency (Montenegro)\") is responsible for counterintelligence and internal security, while Interpol Montenegro collaborates with international agencies to counter transnational crime. Special units within the police, such as the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit (SAJ), handle organized crime, terrorism, and high-risk operations.\\n\\nAn agreement signed with the [EU](/wiki/EU \"EU\") effective July 2023 permits EU [Frontex](/wiki/Frontex \"Frontex\") border management personnel to operate in Montenegro in support of local border police operating on other, non EU, borders in Montenegro.[[148]](#cite_note-154)\\n\\nEmergency services in Montenegro include medical services, firefighters, and search and rescue units, which are coordinated by the Directorate for Emergency Situations. Emergency medical services are operated by local health institutions but are overseen by the [Ministry of Health](/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Montenegro) \"Ministry of Health (Montenegro)\").\\n\\n### Military\\n\\nMain article: [Armed Forces of Montenegro](/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_Montenegro \"Armed Forces of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Final_formation_%287168937179%29.jpg/250px-Final_formation_%287168937179%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Final_formation_(7168937179).jpg)\\n\\n[Montenegrin army soldiers](/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_Montenegro \"Armed Forces of Montenegro\") with [NATO](/wiki/NATO \"NATO\") allies in [Slunj](/wiki/Slunj \"Slunj\"), [Croatia](/wiki/Croatia \"Croatia\")\\n\\nThe military of Montenegro consist of three professional service branches: the [Montenegrin Ground Army](/wiki/Montenegrin_Ground_Army \"Montenegrin Ground Army\"), the [Montenegrin Navy](/wiki/Montenegrin_Navy \"Montenegrin Navy\") and the [Montenegrin Air Force](/wiki/Montenegrin_Air_Force \"Montenegrin Air Force\"). The armed forces of Montenegro are managed by the [Ministry of Defence](/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(Montenegro) \"Ministry of Defence (Montenegro)\"), and controlled by the Chief of the General Staff. The [President of Montenegro](/wiki/President_of_Montenegro \"President of Montenegro\") is the [Commander-in-Chief](/wiki/Commander-in-Chief \"Commander-in-Chief\") of the armed forces, to whom members of the forces swear an oath of allegiance. The Armed Forces are charged with protecting Montenegro, promoting the global security interests and supporting international peacekeeping efforts.\\n\\nMontenegro is a NATO member and a member of [Adriatic Charter](/wiki/Adriatic_Charter \"Adriatic Charter\").[[149]](#cite_note-155)[[150]](#cite_note-156) The government planned to have the army participate in [peacekeeping](/wiki/Peacekeeping \"Peacekeeping\") missions through the UN and NATO such as the [International Security Assistance Force](/wiki/International_Security_Assistance_Force \"International Security Assistance Force\").[[151]](#cite_note-157)\\n\\nMontenegro is the 35th most peaceful country in the world, according to the 2024 [Global Peace Index](/wiki/Global_Peace_Index \"Global Peace Index\").[[152]](#cite_note-158)\\n\\nEconomy\\n-------\\n\\nMain article: [Economy of Montenegro](/wiki/Economy_of_Montenegro \"Economy of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Krnovo_Wind_farm_07.jpg/250px-Krnovo_Wind_farm_07.jpg)](/wiki/File:Krnovo_Wind_farm_07.jpg)\\n\\nKrnovo Wind farm\\n\\nThe economy of Montenegro is mostly [service-based](/wiki/Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy \"Tertiary sector of the economy\") and is in [late transition](/wiki/Transition_economy \"Transition economy\") to a [market economy](/wiki/Market_economy \"Market economy\"). According to the [International Monetary Fund](/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund \"International Monetary Fund\"), the [nominal GDP](/wiki/Nominal_GDP \"Nominal GDP\") of Montenegro was $5.424\\xa0billion in 2019.[[153]](#cite_note-IMFWEO.ME-159) The [GDP PPP](/wiki/GDP_PPP \"GDP PPP\") for 2019 was $12.516\\xa0billion, or $20,083 per capita.[[153]](#cite_note-IMFWEO.ME-159) According to [Eurostat](/wiki/Eurostat \"Eurostat\") data, the Montenegrin GDP per capita stood at 48% of the EU average in 2018.[[154]](#cite_note-160)\\n\\nMontenegro joined the [Central European Free Trade Agreement](/wiki/Central_European_Free_Trade_Agreement \"Central European Free Trade Agreement\") in 2007 and has a free trade agreement with the [European Free Trade Association](/wiki/European_Free_Trade_Association \"European Free Trade Association\") since 2012. The [Central Bank of Montenegro](/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Montenegro \"Central Bank of Montenegro\") is not part of the euro system but the country is \"[euroised](/wiki/Euroisation \"Euroisation\")\", using [the euro unilaterally](/wiki/Montenegro_and_the_euro \"Montenegro and the euro\") as its currency. Montenegro was ranked 64th in the [Global Innovation Index](/wiki/Global_Innovation_Index \"Global Innovation Index\") in 2025,[[155]](#cite_note-161)[[156]](#cite_note-162) up from 75th in 2023.[[157]](#cite_note-163)\\n\\n### Infrastructure\\n\\nMain article: [Transport in Montenegro](/wiki/Transport_in_Montenegro \"Transport in Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Montenegro_motorways.JPG/250px-Montenegro_motorways.JPG)](/wiki/File:Montenegro_motorways.JPG)\\n\\nRoads of Montenegro in service and planned\\n\\nThe Montenegrin road infrastructure is not at Western European standards. No roads meet full motorway standards. Construction of new motorways is considered a national priority, as they are important for uniform economic development and the development of Montenegro as an attractive tourist destination.\\n\\nThe [European routes](/wiki/European_route \"European route\") that pass through Montenegro are [E65](/wiki/European_route_E65 \"European route E65\") and [E80](/wiki/European_route_E80 \"European route E80\").\\n\\nThe backbone of the Montenegrin rail network is the [Belgrade–Bar railway](/wiki/Belgrade%E2%80%93Bar_railway \"Belgrade–Bar railway\"), which provides international connection towards [Serbia](/wiki/Serbia \"Serbia\"). A domestic branch line, the [Nikšić-Podgorica railway](/wiki/Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87-Podgorica_railway \"Nikšić-Podgorica railway\"), operated as a freight-only line for decades, that opened for passenger traffic after reconstruction and electrification in 2012. The other branch line from Podgorica towards the Albanian border, the [Podgorica–Shkodër railway](/wiki/Podgorica%E2%80%93Shkod%C3%ABr_railway \"Podgorica–Shkodër railway\"), is not in use.\\n\\nMontenegro has two international airports, [Podgorica Airport](/wiki/Podgorica_Airport \"Podgorica Airport\") and [Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport \"Tivat Airport\").\\n\\nThe [Port of Bar](/wiki/Port_of_Bar \"Port of Bar\") is Montenegro\\'s main seaport. Initially built in 1906, the port was almost completely destroyed during World War II. Reconstruction began in 1950. It is equipped to handle over five million tons of cargo annually, but has been operating at a loss and well below capacity. The reconstruction of the [Belgrade-Bar railway](/wiki/Belgrade-Bar_railway \"Belgrade-Bar railway\") and the proposed [Belgrade-Bar motorway](/wiki/Belgrade-Bar_motorway \"Belgrade-Bar motorway\") are expected to return operating levels to capacity.\\n\\nIn 2023 there is a plan to install an [LNG](/wiki/LNG \"LNG\") terminal at Bar to receive gas imports.[[158]](#cite_note-164)\\n\\n### Tourism\\n\\nMain article: [Tourism in Montenegro](/wiki/Tourism_in_Montenegro \"Tourism in Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/The_Black_Lake_in_Montenegro.jpg/250px-The_Black_Lake_in_Montenegro.jpg)](/wiki/File:The_Black_Lake_in_Montenegro.jpg)\\n\\nThe [Black Lake](/wiki/Black_Lake_(Montenegro) \"Black Lake (Montenegro)\") in [Durmitor National Park](/wiki/Durmitor_National_Park \"Durmitor National Park\"), a [World Heritage Site](/wiki/World_Heritage_Site \"World Heritage Site\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Sveti_Stefan_Montenegro_may_2021_%2810%29.jpg/250px-Sveti_Stefan_Montenegro_may_2021_%2810%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Sveti_Stefan_Montenegro_may_2021_(10).jpg)\\n\\n[Sveti Stefan](/wiki/Sveti_Stefan \"Sveti Stefan\")\\n\\nA total of 2.1\\xa0million visitors visited Montenegro in 2022 spending 12.4m nights there.[[159]](#cite_note-165) The majority of foreign visitors to Montenegro come from the neighbouring countries of Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo, as well as Russia.[[160]](#cite_note-166)\\n\\nThe Montenegrin [Adriatic](/wiki/Adriatic \"Adriatic\") coast is 295\\xa0km (183\\xa0mi) long, with 72\\xa0km (45\\xa0mi) of beaches and many well-preserved ancient towns. Some of the most popular beaches include [Jaz Beach](/wiki/Jaz_Beach \"Jaz Beach\"), [Mogren Beach](/wiki/Budva \"Budva\"), [Bečići Beach](/wiki/Be%C4%8Di%C4%87i \"Bečići\"), [Sveti Stefan Beach](/wiki/Sveti_Stefan \"Sveti Stefan\") and [Velika Plaža](/wiki/Velika_Pla%C5%BEa \"Velika Plaža\").[[161]](#cite_note-My_Guide_Montenegro-167) Meanwhile, some of the most popular ancient towns include [Herceg Novi](/wiki/Herceg_Novi \"Herceg Novi\"), [Perast](/wiki/Perast \"Perast\"), [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\"), [Budva](/wiki/Budva \"Budva\") and [Ulcinj](/wiki/Ulcinj \"Ulcinj\").[[162]](#cite_note-My_Guide_Montenegro_2020-168)\\n\\n*[National Geographic Traveler](/wiki/National_Geographic_Traveler \"National Geographic Traveler\")* (edited once a decade) ranks Montenegro among the \"50 Places of a Lifetime\". Montenegrin seaside town [Sveti Stefan](/wiki/Sveti_Stefan \"Sveti Stefan\") was once used as the cover for the magazine.[[163]](#cite_note-169) The coast region of Montenegro was considered one of the great \"discoveries\" among world tourists. In January 2010, *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times \"The New York Times\")* ranked the Ulcinj South Coast region of Montenegro, including [Velika Plaža](/wiki/Velika_Pla%C5%BEa \"Velika Plaža\"), [Ada Bojana](/wiki/Ada_Bojana \"Ada Bojana\"), and the [Hotel Mediteran](/wiki/Hotel_Mediteran \"Hotel Mediteran\") of Ulcinj, among the \"Top 31 Places to Go in 2010\" as part of a worldwide ranking.[[164]](#cite_note-170)\\n\\nDemographics\\n------------\\n\\nMain articles: [Demographics of Montenegro](/wiki/Demographics_of_Montenegro \"Demographics of Montenegro\") and [Demographic history of Montenegro](/wiki/Demographic_history_of_Montenegro \"Demographic history of Montenegro\")\\n\\n### Ethnic structure\\n\\nThe 2023 census reported 623,633 citizens.[[165]](#cite_note-t819-171) Montenegro is a [multiethnic state](/wiki/Multiethnic_state \"Multiethnic state\") with no ethnic majority.[[166]](#cite_note-172)[[167]](#cite_note-173) [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins \"Montenegrins\") make up 41.1% of the population, [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro \"Serbs of Montenegro\") 32.9%, [Bosniaks](/wiki/Bosniaks_of_Montenegro \"Bosniaks of Montenegro\") 9.45%, [Albanians](/wiki/Albanians_in_Montenegro \"Albanians in Montenegro\") 4.99%, and [Russians](/wiki/Russians \"Russians\") 2.01%.[[168]](#cite_note-g302-174) There is a significant number of other ethnic groups, including [Romani people](/wiki/Romani_people_in_Montenegro \"Romani people in Montenegro\"), [Croats](/wiki/Croats_in_Montenegro \"Croats in Montenegro\"), [Ukrainians](/wiki/Ukrainians \"Ukrainians\"), [Belarusians](/wiki/Belarusians \"Belarusians\"), and [Turks](/wiki/Turkish_people \"Turkish people\").\\n\\n### Languages\\n\\nMain article: [Languages of Montenegro](/wiki/Languages_of_Montenegro \"Languages of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Be%C4%8Dko_izdanje_Gorskog_vijenca_1847.png/250px-Be%C4%8Dko_izdanje_Gorskog_vijenca_1847.png)](/wiki/File:Be%C4%8Dko_izdanje_Gorskog_vijenca_1847.png)\\n\\n[The Mountain Wreath](/wiki/The_Mountain_Wreath \"The Mountain Wreath\") is a poetic chronicle documenting the struggle of the Montenegrin people for independence from the Ottoman Empire, and is the most famous literary work in the country.\\n\\nThe official language in Montenegro is [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language \"Montenegrin language\"). [Serbian](/wiki/Serbian_language \"Serbian language\"), [Bosnian](/wiki/Bosnian_language \"Bosnian language\"), [Albanian](/wiki/Albanian_language \"Albanian language\"), and [Croatian](/wiki/Croatian_language \"Croatian language\") are recognised in official usage. Montenegrin, Serbian, Bosnian, and Croatian are [mutually intelligible](/wiki/Mutually_intelligible \"Mutually intelligible\") as [standard varieties](/wiki/Standard_varieties \"Standard varieties\") of the [Serbo-Croatian language](/wiki/Serbo-Croatian_language \"Serbo-Croatian language\"). Serbian is the most spoken language in the country, as a plurality of the population at 43.18% consider it as their [native language](/wiki/Native_language \"Native language\"), while 34.52% speaks the Montenegrin language. There is also significant number of people speaking Bosnian (6.98%), Albanian (5.25%), and [Russian](/wiki/Russian_language \"Russian language\") (2.36%).[[169]](#cite_note-q454-175)\\n\\n### Religion\\n\\nMain article: [Religion in Montenegro](/wiki/Religion_in_Montenegro \"Religion in Montenegro\")\\n\\nReligion in Montenegro ([ARDA](/wiki/Association_of_Religion_Data_Archives \"Association of Religion Data Archives\") 2020 est.)[[170]](#cite_note-176)\\n\\n1. [Orthodox](/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox \"Eastern Orthodox\") (70.7%)\\n2. [Catholic](/wiki/Catholic \"Catholic\") (2.96%)\\n3. [Protestant](/wiki/Protestant \"Protestant\") (2.91%)\\n4. [Other Christian](/wiki/Christianity \"Christianity\") (2.15%)\\n5. [Sunni](/wiki/Sunni \"Sunni\") (17.9%)\\n6. [None](/wiki/Irreligion \"Irreligion\") (3.43%)\\n7. Other (0.01%)\\n\\nMontenegro has historically stood at the crossroads of multiculturalism, and over centuries this has shaped its unique co-existence between its Christian and Muslim populations.[[171]](#cite_note-177) Montenegrins have throughout history been [Eastern Orthodox Christians](/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Christians \"Eastern Orthodox Christians\") that are members of the [Serbian Orthodox Church](/wiki/Serbian_Orthodox_Church \"Serbian Orthodox Church\"), which is governed by the [Metropolitanate of Montenegro and the Littoral](/wiki/Metropolitanate_of_Montenegro_and_the_Littoral \"Metropolitanate of Montenegro and the Littoral\") and the [Eparchy of Budimlja and Nikšić](/wiki/Eparchy_of_Budimlja_and_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 \"Eparchy of Budimlja and Nikšić\").[[172]](#cite_note-Evropa_2021_i808-178) [Eastern Orthodox Christianity](/wiki/Eastern_Orthodoxy_in_Montenegro \"Eastern Orthodoxy in Montenegro\") is the predominant religion in Montenegro, with 71.1% of the population adhering to the religion.[[173]](#cite_note-p282-179) Meanwhile, the Serbian Orthodox Church is the largest and most popular church, with approximately 90% of Orthodox Christians in Montenegro following the church.[[174]](#cite_note-United_States_Department_of_State_2021_x826-180) A [schismatic](/wiki/Schism_in_Christianity \"Schism in Christianity\") church called The [Montenegrin Orthodox Church](/wiki/Montenegrin_Orthodox_Church \"Montenegrin Orthodox Church\"), which broke off from the Serbian Orthodox church in 1993, is followed by the remaining 10% of Orthodox Christians in the country. It also has not been officially recognised by the [Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople](/wiki/Ecumenical_Patriarchate_of_Constantinople \"Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople\") and is not in communion with any other canonical Orthodox Christian Church.[[175]](#cite_note-vijesti.me_2019_u217-181)\\n\\nDespite tensions between religious groups during the [Bosnian War](/wiki/Bosnian_War \"Bosnian War\"), Montenegro remained fairly stable, mainly due to its population\\'s perspective on religious tolerance and faith diversity.[[176]](#cite_note-182) Religious institutions have guaranteed rights and are separate from the state. The second largest religion is [Islam](/wiki/Islam_in_Montenegro \"Islam in Montenegro\"), practiced by 19% of the population. Montenegro has one of the highest proportion of Muslims in Europe and the third highest proportion among Slavic countries, behind only Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia. A little more than one-fourth of the country\\'s [Albanians](/wiki/Albanians \"Albanians\") are [Catholics](/wiki/Catholics \"Catholics\") (8,126 in the 2003 census) while the rest (22,267) are mainly [Sunni Muslims](/wiki/Sunni_Muslims \"Sunni Muslims\"); in 2012 a protocol recognised [Islam](/wiki/Islam \"Islam\") as an official religion, which ensures that [halal](/wiki/Halal \"Halal\") foods are served at military facilities, hospitals, dormitories and social facilities; and that Muslim women are permitted to wear headscarves in schools and at public institutions, as well as ensuring that Muslims have the right to take Fridays off for the [Jumu\\'ah](/wiki/Jumu%27ah \"Jumu\\'ah\") (Friday)-prayer.[[177]](#cite_note-183) Since the time of [Vojislavljević dynasty](/wiki/Vojislavljevi%C4%87_dynasty \"Vojislavljević dynasty\") Catholicism is autochthonous in the Montenegrin area.[[178]](#cite_note-184) A small Roman Catholic population, mostly Albanians with some Croats, is divided between the [Archdiocese of Antivari](/wiki/Archdiocese_of_Antivari \"Archdiocese of Antivari\") headed by the Primate of Serbia and the [Diocese of Kotor](/wiki/Diocese_of_Kotor \"Diocese of Kotor\") that is a part of the [Catholic Church in Croatia](/wiki/Catholic_Church_in_Croatia \"Catholic Church in Croatia\").\\n\\nCulture\\n-------\\n\\nMain article: [Culture of Montenegro](/wiki/Culture_of_Montenegro \"Culture of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/2023_Cetinje_National_Museum.jpg/250px-2023_Cetinje_National_Museum.jpg)](/wiki/File:2023_Cetinje_National_Museum.jpg)\\n\\n[National Museum of Montenegro](/wiki/National_Museum_of_Montenegro \"National Museum of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Tripundan_2023_%2804%29.jpg/250px-Tripundan_2023_%2804%29.jpg)](/wiki/File:Tripundan_2023_(04).jpg)\\n\\nBoka Navy, from 2021 part of intangible [World Heritage](/wiki/World_Heritage \"World Heritage\") UNESCO\\n\\nMontenegrin culture has been shaped most importantly by Orthodox, Ottoman (Turk), Slavic, Central European, and seafaring Adriatic cultures (notably parts of Italy, like the [Republic of Venice](/wiki/Republic_of_Venice \"Republic of Venice\")).\\n\\nMontenegro has many significant cultural and historical sites, including heritage sites from the pre-[Romanesque](/wiki/Romanesque_architecture \"Romanesque architecture\"), [Gothic](/wiki/Gothic_art \"Gothic art\") and [Baroque](/wiki/Baroque \"Baroque\") periods. The Montenegrin coastal region is known for its religious monuments, including the [Cathedral of Saint Tryphon](/wiki/Cathedral_of_Saint_Tryphon \"Cathedral of Saint Tryphon\") in [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\")[[179]](#cite_note-185) (Cattaro under the Venetians), the basilica of St. Luke (over 800 years), [Our Lady of the Rocks](/wiki/Our_Lady_of_the_Rocks \"Our Lady of the Rocks\") (Škrpjela), the [Savina Monastery](/wiki/Savina_monastery_(Montenegro) \"Savina monastery (Montenegro)\") and others. Medieval monasteries contain many artistically important frescoes.\\n\\nOne cultural dimension is the ethical ideal of *Čojstvo i Junaštvo*, \"Humaneness and Gallantry\".[[180]](#cite_note-186)[[181]](#cite_note-187) The traditional folk dance of the Montenegrins is the [Oro](/wiki/Oro_(eagle_dance) \"Oro (eagle dance)\"), the \"eagle dance\" that involves dancing in circles with couples alternating in the centre, and is finished by forming a human pyramid of dancers standing on each other\\'s shoulders.\\n\\n### Media\\n\\nMain article: [Media of Montenegro](/wiki/Media_of_Montenegro \"Media of Montenegro\")\\n\\nTelevision, magazines, and newspapers are operated by both state-owned and for-profit corporations that depend on advertising, [subscription](/wiki/Subscription \"Subscription\"), and other sales-related revenues. The [Constitution of Montenegro](/wiki/Constitution_of_Montenegro \"Constitution of Montenegro\") guarantees freedom of speech. Montenegro\\'s media system is under transformation, along with the rest of the country. The privately owned media outlet [Vijesti](/wiki/Vijesti \"Vijesti\") (*News*) has been the most watched in Montenegro for many years, followed by the state-owned [Radio and Television of Montenegro](/wiki/Radio_and_Television_of_Montenegro \"Radio and Television of Montenegro\") (*Radio-televizija Crne Gore, RTCG*).[[3]](https://www.vijesti.me/tv/emisije/739131/televizija-vijesti-sestu-godinu-zaredom-najgledanija-u-crnoj-gori) *RTCG* also provides radio and television broadcasts of daily news in the Albanian language.\\n\\n### Sport\\n\\nMain article: [Sport in Montenegro](/wiki/Sport_in_Montenegro \"Sport in Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Sports_Center_Moraca.jpg/250px-Sports_Center_Moraca.jpg)](/wiki/File:Sports_Center_Moraca.jpg)\\n\\nExterior of the [Morača Sports Center](/wiki/Mora%C4%8Da_Sports_Center \"Morača Sports Center\")\\n\\nSport in Montenegro revolves mostly around [team sports](/wiki/Team_sport \"Team sport\"), such as [water polo](/wiki/Water_polo \"Water polo\"), [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\"), [basketball](/wiki/Basketball \"Basketball\"), [handball](/wiki/Handball \"Handball\"), and [volleyball](/wiki/Volleyball \"Volleyball\"). Other sports involved are [boxing](/wiki/Boxing \"Boxing\"), [tennis](/wiki/Tennis \"Tennis\"), swimming, [judo](/wiki/Judo \"Judo\"), [karate](/wiki/Karate \"Karate\"), [athletics](/wiki/Athletics_(sport) \"Athletics (sport)\"), [table tennis](/wiki/Table_tennis \"Table tennis\"), and [chess](/wiki/Chess \"Chess\").\\n\\n[Water polo](/wiki/Water_polo \"Water polo\") is the most popular and is considered the [national sport](/wiki/National_sport \"National sport\").[[182]](#cite_note-Popular_Sports-188) [Montenegro men\\'s national water polo team](/wiki/Montenegro_men%27s_national_water_polo_team \"Montenegro men\\'s national water polo team\") is one of the world\\'s [top ranked](/wiki/FINA_Water_Polo_World_Rankings \"FINA Water Polo World Rankings\") teams, winning the gold medal at the [2008 Men\\'s European Water Polo Championship](/wiki/2008_Men%27s_European_Water_Polo_Championship \"2008 Men\\'s European Water Polo Championship\") in [Málaga](/wiki/M%C3%A1laga \"Málaga\"), Spain, and winning the gold medal at the [2009 FINA Men\\'s Water Polo World League](/wiki/2009_FINA_Men%27s_Water_Polo_World_League \"2009 FINA Men\\'s Water Polo World League\"), held in [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica \"Podgorica\"). The Montenegrin team [PVK Primorac](/wiki/PVK_Primorac \"PVK Primorac\") from [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\") became a champion of Europe at the [LEN Euroleague](/wiki/LEN_Euroleague \"LEN Euroleague\") 2009 in [Rijeka](/wiki/Rijeka \"Rijeka\"), Croatia. Montenegro came fourth in the men\\'s water polo in the [2016 Olympics](/wiki/Water_polo_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics \"Water polo at the 2016 Summer Olympics\").\\n\\n[Football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") is the second most popular sport.[[182]](#cite_note-Popular_Sports-188) The [Montenegro national football team](/wiki/Montenegro_national_football_team \"Montenegro national football team\"), founded in 2006, played in playoffs for [UEFA Euro 2012](/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2012 \"UEFA Euro 2012\"), its highest play appearance. The [Montenegro national basketball team](/wiki/Montenegro_national_basketball_team \"Montenegro national basketball team\") is known for good performances and won many medals as part of the [Yugoslavia national basketball team](/wiki/Yugoslavia_national_basketball_team \"Yugoslavia national basketball team\"). In 2006, the [Basketball Federation of Montenegro](/wiki/Basketball_Federation_of_Montenegro \"Basketball Federation of Montenegro\") along with this team joined the [International Basketball Federation](/wiki/International_Basketball_Federation \"International Basketball Federation\") (FIBA) on its own, following the [Independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"). Montenegro participated in two [EuroBaskets](/wiki/EuroBasket \"EuroBasket\").\\n\\nAmong women sports, [the national handball team](/wiki/Montenegro_women%27s_national_handball_team \"Montenegro women\\'s national handball team\") is the most successful, winning the country\\'s first Olympic medal, claiming silver at the [2012 Summer Olympics](/wiki/Handball_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics \"Handball at the 2012 Summer Olympics\"). This was followed by the [2012 European Championship](/wiki/2012_European_Women%27s_Handball_Championship \"2012 European Women\\'s Handball Championship\") which Montenegro won, becoming European champions. [ŽRK Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/%C5%BDRK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica \"ŽRK Budućnost Podgorica\") has twice won the EHF Champions League. Montenegro was one of the host countries for the [2022 European Women\\'s Handball Championship](/wiki/2022_European_Women%27s_Handball_Championship \"2022 European Women\\'s Handball Championship\") and came third.\\n\\n### Cuisine\\n\\nMain article: [Montenegrin cuisine](/wiki/Montenegrin_cuisine \"Montenegrin cuisine\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Foods_from_Montenegro.jpg/250px-Foods_from_Montenegro.jpg)](/wiki/File:Foods_from_Montenegro.jpg)\\n\\nFoods from Montenegro\\n\\nThe first major influences to Montenegrin cuisine came from the [Levant](/wiki/Levant \"Levant\") and [Turkey](/wiki/Turkish_cuisine \"Turkish cuisine\"): [sarma](/wiki/Sarma_(food) \"Sarma (food)\"), [musaka](/wiki/Musaka \"Musaka\"), [pilav](/wiki/Pilav \"Pilav\"), [pita](/wiki/B%C3%B6rek#Balkans \"Börek\"), [gibanica](/wiki/Gibanica \"Gibanica\"), [burek](/wiki/Burek \"Burek\"), [ćevapi](/wiki/%C4%86evapi \"Ćevapi\"), [kebab](/wiki/Kebab \"Kebab\"), [đuveč](/wiki/%C4%90uve%C4%8D \"Đuveč\"), and Turkish sweets such as [baklava](/wiki/Baklava \"Baklava\") and [tulumba](/wiki/Tulumba \"Tulumba\"). [Hungarian cuisine](/wiki/Hungarian_cuisine \"Hungarian cuisine\") influences [stews](/wiki/Goulash \"Goulash\") and [sataraš](/wiki/Satara%C5%A1 \"Sataraš\"). [Central European cuisine](/wiki/Central_European_cuisine \"Central European cuisine\") is evident in the prevalence of [crêpes](/wiki/Cr%C3%AApes \"Crêpes\"), [doughnuts](/wiki/Doughnuts \"Doughnuts\"), [jams](/wiki/Jam \"Jam\"), many types of [biscuits](/wiki/Biscuits \"Biscuits\") and [cakes](/wiki/Cakes \"Cakes\"), and various kinds of breads. Montenegrin cuisine also varies geographically; with the cuisine in the coastal area differing from that of the northern highland region. The coastal area is traditionally a representative of [Mediterranean cuisine](/wiki/Mediterranean_cuisine \"Mediterranean cuisine\"), with [seafood](/wiki/Seafood \"Seafood\") being a common dish. The traditional dishes of Montenegro\\'s [Adriatic coast](/wiki/Adriatic_coast \"Adriatic coast\"), unlike its heartland, have been significantly influenced by [Italian](/wiki/Italian_cuisine \"Italian cuisine\") cuisine.[[183]](#cite_note-189)\\n\\nSee also\\n--------\\n\\n* **Bosnia and Herzegovina**,[[a]](#cite_note-18)[[b]](#cite_note-19) often referred to as **Bosnia-Herzegovina** or simply as **Bosnia**, is a country in [Southeast Europe](/wiki/Southeast_Europe "Southeast Europe"). Situated on the [Balkan Peninsula](/wiki/Balkans "Balkans"), it borders [Serbia](/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") to the east, [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") to the southeast, and [Croatia](/wiki/Croatia "Croatia") to the north and southwest, with a 20-kilometre-long (12-mile) coast on the [Adriatic Sea](/wiki/Adriatic_Sea "Adriatic Sea") in the south. [Bosnia](/wiki/Bosnia_(region) "Bosnia (region)") has a moderate [continental climate](/wiki/Continental_climate "Continental climate") with hot summers and cold, snowy winters. Its geography is largely mountainous, particularly in the central and eastern regions, which are dominated by the [Dinaric Alps](/wiki/Dinaric_Alps "Dinaric Alps"). [Herzegovina](/wiki/Herzegovina "Herzegovina"), the smaller, southern region, has a [Mediterranean climate](/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate") and is mostly mountainous. [Sarajevo](/wiki/Sarajevo "Sarajevo") is the capital and the largest city.

The area has been inhabited since at least the [Upper Palaeolithic](/wiki/Upper_Palaeolithic "Upper Palaeolithic"), with permanent human settlement traced to the [Neolithic](/wiki/Neolithic "Neolithic") cultures of [Butmir](/wiki/Butmir_culture "Butmir culture"), [Kakanj](/wiki/Kakanj_culture "Kakanj culture"), and [Vučedol](/wiki/Vu%C4%8Dedol_culture "Vučedol culture"). After the arrival of the first [Indo-Europeans](/wiki/Proto-Indo-Europeans "Proto-Indo-Europeans"), the area was populated by several [Illyrian](/wiki/Illyria "Illyria") and [Celtic](/wiki/Celts "Celts") civilisations. Most of modern Bosnia was incorporated into the [Roman province of Dalmatia](/wiki/Dalmatia_(Roman_province) "Dalmatia (Roman province)") by the mid-first century BCE. The [ancestors of the modern South Slavic peoples](/wiki/Early_Slavs "Early Slavs") arrived between the sixth and ninth centuries. In the 12th century, the [Banate of Bosnia](/wiki/Banate_of_Bosnia "Banate of Bosnia") was established as the first independent Bosnian [polity](/wiki/Polity "Polity").[[17]](#cite_note-:0-20) It gradually evolved and expanded into the [Kingdom of Bosnia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Bosnia "Kingdom of Bosnia"), which became the most powerful state in the western Balkans by the 14th century.[[17]](#cite_note-:0-20) The [Ottoman Empire](/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") [annexed the region](/wiki/Ottoman_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Ottoman Bosnia and Herzegovina") in 1463 and introduced [Islam](/wiki/Islam_in_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Islam in Bosnia and Herzegovina"). From the late 19th century until [World War I](/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), the country was [annexed into the Austro-Hungarian monarchy](/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_rule_in_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Austro-Hungarian rule in Bosnia and Herzegovina"). In the [interwar period](/wiki/Interwar_period "Interwar period"), Bosnia and Herzegovina was part of the [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia "Kingdom of Yugoslavia"). After [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), it was granted full republic status in the newly formed [Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia"). In 1992, following the [breakup of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia"), [the republic proclaimed independence](/wiki/1992_Bosnian_independence_referendum "1992 Bosnian independence referendum"). This was followed by the [Bosnian War](/wiki/Bosnian_War "Bosnian War"), which lasted until late 1995 and ended with the signing of the [Dayton Agreement](/wiki/Dayton_Agreement "Dayton Agreement").

Bosnia and Herzegovina has roughly 2.9 million inhabitants based on the current estimates, composed chiefly of [three main ethnic groups](/wiki/Ethnic_groups_in_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Ethnic groups in Bosnia and Herzegovina"): [Bosniaks](/wiki/Bosniaks "Bosniaks"), who form more than a half of the population, followed by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Serbs of Bosnia and Herzegovina") at one-third and [Croats](/wiki/Croats_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Croats of Bosnia and Herzegovina") at one-sixth; minorities include [Jews](/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "History of the Jews in Bosnia and Herzegovina"), [Roma](/wiki/Romani_people_in_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Romani people in Bosnia and Herzegovina"), [Albanians, Montenegrins, Ukrainians and Turks](/wiki/National_minorities_in_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "National minorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina"), who are among 17 recognized "national minorities". Bosnia and Herzegovina has a [bicameral](/wiki/Bicameralism "Bicameralism") legislature and a [presidency](/wiki/Presidency_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina") made up of one member from each of the three major ethnic groups ([directorial system](/wiki/Directorial_system "Directorial system")). The central government's power is minimal, as the country is largely decentralised; it comprises two autonomous entities—the [Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina](/wiki/Federation_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina") and [Republika Srpska](/wiki/Republika_Srpska "Republika Srpska")—and a third unit, the [Brčko District](/wiki/Br%C4%8Dko_District "Brčko District"), governed by its own local government.

Bosnia and Herzegovina is a [developing country](/wiki/Developing_country "Developing country") and [an upper-middle income economy](/wiki/Economy_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Economy of Bosnia and Herzegovina"), dominated by industry and agriculture, followed by tourism and [services](/wiki/Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy "Tertiary sector of the economy"); tourism has increased significantly in recent years.[[18]](#cite_note-21)[[19]](#cite_note-22) The country has a [social security](/wiki/Welfare_spending "Welfare spending") and universal healthcare system, while [primary and secondary education](/wiki/Education_in_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Education in Bosnia and Herzegovina") is free. It is a member of the [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations"), [Council of Europe](/wiki/Council_of_Europe "Council of Europe"), [OSCE](/wiki/Organization_for_Security_and_Co-operation_in_Europe "Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe"), [CEFTA](/wiki/Central_European_Free_Trade_Agreement "Central European Free Trade Agreement"), and is also a founding member of the [SEECP](/wiki/South-East_European_Cooperation_Process "South-East European Cooperation Process"). Bosnia and Herzegovina has been an [EU candidate country](/wiki/Accession_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_to_the_European_Union "Accession of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the European Union") since 2022, and a [NATO](/wiki/NATO "NATO") membership candidate since 2010.[[20]](#cite_note-23)

Etymology
---------

The first preserved widely acknowledged mention of a form of the name "[Bosnia](/wiki/Bosnia_(region) "Bosnia (region)")" is in *[De Administrando Imperio](/wiki/De_Administrando_Imperio "De Administrando Imperio")*, a politico-geographical handbook written by the [Byzantine emperor](/wiki/List_of_Byzantine_emperors "List of Byzantine emperors") [Constantine VII](/wiki/Constantine_VII "Constantine VII") in the mid-10th century (between 948 and 952) describing the "small land" (χωρίον) in [Greek](/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language") of "Bosona" (Βοσώνα).[[21]](#cite_note-Moravcsik-153-24)

The name of the land is believed to derive from the name of the river [Bosna](/wiki/Bosna_(river) "Bosna (river)") that courses through the Bosnian heartland. According to [philologist](/wiki/Philology "Philology") Anton Mayer, the name *Bosna* could derive from [Illyrian](/wiki/Illyrian_language "Illyrian language") \*"Bass-an-as", which in turn could derive from the Proto-Indo-European root *[bʰegʷ-](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Reconstruction:Proto-Indo-European/b%CA%B0eg%CA%B7- "wikt:Reconstruction:Proto-Indo-European/bʰegʷ-")*, meaning "the running water".[[22]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMalcolm2002-25)

The name *Herzegovina* means "herzog's [land]", and "herzog" derives from the German word for "duke".[[22]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMalcolm2002-25) It originates from the title of a 15th-century Bosnian magnate, [Stjepan Vukčić Kosača](/wiki/Stjepan_Vuk%C4%8Di%C4%87_Kosa%C4%8Da "Stjepan Vukčić Kosača"), who was "Herceg [Herzog] of Hum and the Coast" (1448).[[23]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFine1994578-26) Hum (formerly called [Zachlumia](/wiki/Zachlumia "Zachlumia")) was an early medieval principality that had been conquered by the Bosnian Banate in the first half of the 14th century. When the Ottomans took over administration of the region, they called it the [Sanjak of Herzegovina](/wiki/Sanjak_of_Herzegovina "Sanjak of Herzegovina") (*Hersek*). It was included within the [Bosnia Eyalet](/wiki/Bosnia_Eyalet "Bosnia Eyalet") until the formation of the short-lived [Herzegovina Eyalet](/wiki/Herzegovina_Eyalet "Herzegovina Eyalet") in the 1830s, which reemerged in the 1850s, after which the administrative region became commonly known as *Bosnia and Herzegovina*.[[24]](#cite_note-Encyclopedia_Britannica-27)

On initial [proclamation of independence in 1992](/wiki/1992_Bosnian_independence_referendum "1992 Bosnian independence referendum"), the country's official name was the [Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina](/wiki/Republic_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina"), but following the 1995 [Dayton Agreement](/wiki/Dayton_Agreement "Dayton Agreement") and the new [constitution](/wiki/Constitution_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina") that accompanied it, the official name was changed to Bosnia and Herzegovina.[*[dubious](/wiki/Wikipedia:Accuracy_dispute#Disputed_statement "Wikipedia:Accuracy dispute") – [discuss](/wiki/Talk:Bosnia_and_Herzegovina#Dubious "Talk:Bosnia and Herzegovina")*][*[why?](/wiki/Wikipedia:Please_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")*][[25]](#cite_note-28)

History
-------
