Track and field athlete [Amel Tuka](/wiki/Amel_Tuka "Amel Tuka") won bronze and silver medals in 800 metres at the [2015](/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics") and [2019 IAAF World Athletics Championships](/wiki/2019_IAAF_World_Athletics_Championships "2019 IAAF World Athletics Championships")[[261]](#cite_note-264) and [Hamza Alić](/wiki/Hamza_Ali%C4%87 "Hamza Alić") won the silver medal in [shot put](/wiki/2013_European_Athletics_Indoor_Championships_%E2%80%93_Men%27s_shot_put "2013 European Athletics Indoor Championships – Men's shot put") at the [2013 European Indoor Championships](/wiki/2013_European_Athletics_Indoor_Championships "2013 European Athletics Indoor Championships").

The [Bosna Royal](/wiki/KK_Bosna_Royal "KK Bosna Royal") [basketball](/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") club from Sarajevo were [European Champions](/wiki/Euroleague_Basketball "Euroleague Basketball") in [1979](/wiki/1978%E2%80%9379_FIBA_European_Champions_Cup "1978–79 FIBA European Champions Cup"). The [Yugoslavia men's national basketball team](/wiki/Yugoslavia_men%27s_national_basketball_team "Yugoslavia men's national basketball team"), which won medals in every world championship from 1963 through 1990, included Bosnian players such as [FIBA Hall of Famers](/wiki/FIBA_Hall_of_Fame "FIBA Hall of Fame") [Dražen Dalipagić](/wiki/Dra%C5%BEen_Dalipagi%C4%87 "Dražen Dalipagić") and [Mirza Delibašić](/wiki/Mirza_Deliba%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Mirza Delibašić"). Bosnia and Herzegovina regularly qualifies for the [European Championship in Basketball](/wiki/EuroBasket "EuroBasket"), with players including [Mirza Teletović](/wiki/Mirza_Teletovi%C4%87 "Mirza Teletović"), [Nihad Đedović](/wiki/Nihad_%C4%90edovi%C4%87 "Nihad Đedović") and [Jusuf Nurkić](/wiki/Jusuf_Nurki%C4%87 "Jusuf Nurkić"). The [Bosnia and Herzegovina national under-16 team](/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_men%27s_national_under-16_and_under-17_basketball_team "Bosnia and Herzegovina men's national under-16 and under-17 basketball team") won two gold medals in 2015, winning both [2015 European Youth Summer Olympic Festival](/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2015_European_Youth_Summer_Olympic_Festival "Basketball at the 2015 European Youth Summer Olympic Festival") as well as the [2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship](/wiki/2015_FIBA_Europe_Under-16_Championship "2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship").

Women's basketball club [Jedinstvo Aida](/wiki/%C5%BDKK_Jedinstvo_Tuzla "ŽKK Jedinstvo Tuzla") from [Tuzla](/wiki/Tuzla "Tuzla") won the [Women's European Club Championship](/wiki/EuroLeague_Women "EuroLeague Women") in 1989 and went to the [Ronchetti Cup](/wiki/Ronchetti_Cup "Ronchetti Cup") final in 1990, led by [Razija Mujanović](/wiki/Razija_Mujanovi%C4%87 "Razija Mujanović").[[262]](#cite_note-265)

The Bosnian [chess](/wiki/Chess "Chess") team was [Champion of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Yugoslav_Chess_Championship "Yugoslav Chess Championship") seven times, in addition to club [ŠK Bosna](/wiki/%C5%A0K_Bosna "ŠK Bosna") winning four [European Chess Club Cups](/wiki/European_Chess_Club_Cup "European Chess Club Cup"). Chess grandmaster [Borki Predojević](/wiki/Borki_Predojevi%C4%87 "Borki Predojević") has also won two European Championships. The most impressive success of Bosnian Chess was a runner-up position at the [31st Chess Olympiad](/wiki/31st_Chess_Olympiad "31st Chess Olympiad") in 1994 in [Moscow](/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), featuring Grandmasters [Predrag Nikolić](/wiki/Predrag_Nikoli%C4%87 "Predrag Nikolić"), [Ivan Sokolov](/wiki/Ivan_Sokolov_(chess_player) "Ivan Sokolov (chess player)") and [Bojan Kurajica](/wiki/Bojan_Kurajica "Bojan Kurajica").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Middle-weight [boxer](/wiki/Boxing "Boxing") [Marijan Beneš](/wiki/Marijan_Bene%C5%A1 "Marijan Beneš") has won several Championships of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Yugoslav Championships and the [European Championship](/wiki/European_Amateur_Boxing_Championships "European Amateur Boxing Championships").[[263]](#cite_note-nezavisne-266) In 1978, he won the World Title against [Elisha Obed](/wiki/Elisha_Obed "Elisha Obed") from [The Bahamas](/wiki/The_Bahamas "The Bahamas").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7f/20150331_2219_AUT_BIH_2704.jpg/250px-20150331_2219_AUT_BIH_2704.jpg)](/wiki/File:20150331_2219_AUT_BIH_2704.jpg)

[Edin Džeko](/wiki/Edin_D%C5%BEeko "Edin Džeko") playing for [Bosnia and Herzegovina](/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_national_football_team "Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team") in 2015

[Association football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") is the most popular sport in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It dates from 1903, but its popularity grew significantly after [World War I](/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"). Bosnian clubs [FK Sarajevo](/wiki/FK_Sarajevo "FK Sarajevo") and [Željezničar](/wiki/FK_%C5%BDeljezni%C4%8Dar_Sarajevo "FK Željezničar Sarajevo") won the [Yugoslav Championship](/wiki/Yugoslav_First_League "Yugoslav First League"), while the [Yugoslav national football team](/wiki/Yugoslavia_national_football_team "Yugoslavia national football team") included Bosnian players of all ethnic backgrounds and generations, such as [Safet Sušić](/wiki/Safet_Su%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Safet Sušić"), [Zlatko Vujović](/wiki/Zlatko_Vujovi%C4%87 "Zlatko Vujović"), [Mehmed Baždarević](/wiki/Mehmed_Ba%C5%BEdarevi%C4%87 "Mehmed Baždarević"), [Davor Jozić](/wiki/Davor_Jozi%C4%87 "Davor Jozić"), [Faruk Hadžibegić](/wiki/Faruk_Had%C5%BEibegi%C4%87 "Faruk Hadžibegić"), [Predrag Pašić](/wiki/Predrag_Pa%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Predrag Pašić"), [Blaž Slišković](/wiki/Bla%C5%BE_Sli%C5%A1kovi%C4%87 "Blaž Slišković"), [Vahid Halilhodžić](/wiki/Vahid_Halilhod%C5%BEi%C4%87 "Vahid Halilhodžić"), [Dušan Bajević](/wiki/Du%C5%A1an_Bajevi%C4%87 "Dušan Bajević"), [Ivica Osim](/wiki/Ivica_Osim "Ivica Osim"), [Josip Katalinski](/wiki/Josip_Katalinski "Josip Katalinski"), [Tomislav Knez](/wiki/Tomislav_Knez "Tomislav Knez"), [Velimir Sombolac](/wiki/Velimir_Sombolac "Velimir Sombolac") and numerous others.

The [Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team](/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_national_football_team "Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team") played at the [2014 FIFA World Cup](/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup "2014 FIFA World Cup"), its first major tournament.[[264]](#cite_note-267) Players on the team again includes notable players of all country's ethnic background, such as then and now captains [Emir Spahić](/wiki/Emir_Spahi%C4%87 "Emir Spahić"), [Zvjezdan Misimović](/wiki/Zvjezdan_Misimovi%C4%87 "Zvjezdan Misimović") and [Edin Džeko](/wiki/Edin_D%C5%BEeko "Edin Džeko"), defenders like [Ognjen Vranješ](/wiki/Ognjen_Vranje%C5%A1 "Ognjen Vranješ"), [Sead Kolašinac](/wiki/Sead_Kola%C5%A1inac "Sead Kolašinac") and [Toni Šunjić](/wiki/Toni_%C5%A0unji%C4%87 "Toni Šunjić"), midfielders like [Miralem Pjanić](/wiki/Miralem_Pjani%C4%87 "Miralem Pjanić") and [Senad Lulić](/wiki/Senad_Luli%C4%87 "Senad Lulić"), striker [Vedad Ibišević](/wiki/Vedad_Ibi%C5%A1evi%C4%87 "Vedad Ibišević"), etc. Former Bosnian footballers include [Hasan Salihamidžić](/wiki/Hasan_Salihamid%C5%BEi%C4%87 "Hasan Salihamidžić"), who became only the second Bosnian to ever win a [UEFA Champions League](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") trophy, after [Elvir Baljić](/wiki/Elvir_Balji%C4%87 "Elvir Baljić"). He made 234 appearances and scored 31 goals for German club [FC Bayern Munich](/wiki/FC_Bayern_Munich "FC Bayern Munich"). [Sergej Barbarez](/wiki/Sergej_Barbarez "Sergej Barbarez"), who played for several clubs in the German [Bundesliga](/wiki/Bundesliga "Bundesliga"). including [Borussia Dortmund](/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund"), [Hamburger SV](/wiki/Hamburger_SV "Hamburger SV") and [Bayer Leverkusen](/wiki/Bayer_04_Leverkusen "Bayer 04 Leverkusen") was joint-top scorer in the [2000–01 Bundesliga](/wiki/2000%E2%80%9301_Bundesliga "2000–01 Bundesliga") season with 22 goals. [Meho Kodro](/wiki/Meho_Kodro "Meho Kodro") spent most of his career playing in Spain, most notably with [Real Sociedad](/wiki/Real_Sociedad "Real Sociedad") and [FC Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"). [Elvir Rahimić](/wiki/Elvir_Rahimi%C4%87 "Elvir Rahimić") made 302 appearances for Russian club [CSKA Moscow](/wiki/PFC_CSKA_Moscow "PFC CSKA Moscow") with whom he won the [UEFA Cup](/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") in [2005](/wiki/2005_UEFA_Cup_Final "2005 UEFA Cup Final").
[Milena Nikolić](/wiki/Milena_Nikoli%C4%87 "Milena Nikolić"), member of the [women's national team](/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_women%27s_national_football_team "Bosnia and Herzegovina women's national football team"), was the [2013–14 UEFA Women's Champions League](/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_UEFA_Women%27s_Champions_League "2013–14 UEFA Women's Champions League") [top scorer](/wiki/UEFA_Women%27s_Champions_League#Top_scorers_by_tournament "UEFA Women's Champions League").[[265]](#cite_note-uefa.com-nikolic-scorer-268)

Bosnia and Herzegovina was the world champion of [volleyball at the 2004 Summer Paralympics](/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_2004_Summer_Paralympics "Volleyball at the 2004 Summer Paralympics") and [volleyball at the 2012 Summer Paralympics](/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_2012_Summer_Paralympics "Volleyball at the 2012 Summer Paralympics"). Many among those on the team lost their legs in the [Bosnian War](/wiki/Bosnian_War "Bosnian War"). Its [national sitting volleyball team](/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_national_sitting_volleyball_team "Bosnia and Herzegovina national sitting volleyball team") is one of the dominant forces in [the sport](/wiki/Sitting_volleyball "Sitting volleyball") worldwide, winning nine European Championships, three World Championships and two [Paralympic](/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_Summer_Paralympics "Volleyball at the Summer Paralympics") gold medals.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

[Tennis](/wiki/Tennis "Tennis") is also gaining a lot of popularity after the recent successes of [Damir Džumhur](/wiki/Damir_D%C5%BEumhur "Damir Džumhur") and [Mirza Bašić](/wiki/Mirza_Ba%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Mirza Bašić") at [Grand Slam](/wiki/Grand_Slam_(tennis) "Grand Slam (tennis)") level. Other notable tennis players who have represented Bosnia and Herzegovina are [Tomislav Brkić](/wiki/Tomislav_Brki%C4%87 "Tomislav Brkić"), [Amer Delić](/wiki/Amer_Deli%C4%87 "Amer Delić") and [Mervana Jugić-Salkić](/wiki/Mervana_Jugi%C4%87-Salki%C4%87 "Mervana Jugić-Salkić").

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Radanovići** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cyrillic "Montenegrin Cyrillic"): Радановићи) is a small town in the [municipality](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Montenegro "Municipalities of Montenegro") of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). The town is also part and largest settlement of historical rural region of [Grbalj](/wiki/Grbalj "Grbalj") at the [coastal region of Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegrin_littoral "Montenegrin littoral"). The town of Radanovići is located near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor") region.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Demographics
------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

The settlement has a population of 752 inhabitants, according 2011 census, and is mainly populated by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro "Serbs of Montenegro") (63.69%), with a significant population of [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins "Montenegrins") (21.14%)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town of Radanovići is situated approximately halfway between two main Montenegrin tourist destinations, [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), on the main road that connects these two. [Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 7.5 km (4.6 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade") throughout the year, and dozens of charter planes land daily at the airport during the summer season.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sports")]

Local football team [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara") and currently compete in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League").

**Kotor** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cyrillic_alphabet "Montenegrin Cyrillic alphabet"): Котор, pronounced [[kɔ̌tɔr]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")), historically known as **Cattaro**[[1]](#cite_note-1) (from [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"), pronounced [[ˈkattaro]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian")), is a town in [Coastal region](/wiki/Coastal_Montenegro "Coastal Montenegro") of [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). It is located in a secluded part of the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor"). The city has a population of 13,347 and is the administrative center of [Kotor Municipality](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality").

The old [Mediterranean](/wiki/Mediterranean "Mediterranean") port of Kotor is surrounded by [fortifications](/wiki/Fortifications_of_Kotor "Fortifications of Kotor") built during the [Venetian](/wiki/Republic_of_Venice "Republic of Venice") period. It is located on the Bay of Kotor (*Boka Kotorska*), one of the most indented parts of the [Adriatic Sea](/wiki/Adriatic_Sea "Adriatic Sea"), which constitutes a [ria](/wiki/Ria "Ria"), meaning a submerged river canyon. Together with the nearly overhanging limestone cliffs of [Orjen](/wiki/Orjen "Orjen") and [Lovćen](/wiki/Lov%C4%87en "Lovćen"), Kotor and its surrounding area form the unique landscape.

Since the early 2000s Kotor has seen an increase in tourists,[[2]](#cite_note-2) many of them coming by [cruise ship](/wiki/Cruise_ship "Cruise ship"). Visitors are attracted to the natural environment of the Bay of Kotor and the old town of Kotor. Kotor is part of the [World Heritage Site](/wiki/World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") dubbed the [Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor](/wiki/Natural_and_Culturo-Historical_Region_of_Kotor "Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor").

The fortified city of Kotor was also included in [UNESCO](/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO")'s World Heritage Site list as part of [Venetian Works of Defence between 16th and 17th centuries: *Stato da Terra* – western *Stato da Mar*](/wiki/Venetian_Works_of_Defence_between_16th_and_17th_centuries:_Stato_da_Terra_%E2%80%93_western_Stato_da_Mar "Venetian Works of Defence between 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar") in 2017.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

### Early history

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

Once populated by the [Illyrians](/wiki/Illyrians "Illyrians"), the exact time of foundation of the first settlement is not known. According to some sources, the oldest settled area dates two millennia back.

The city, first mentioned in 168 BC, was settled during [ancient Roman](/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") times, when it was known as **Acruvium**, **Ascrivium**, or **Ascruvium** ([Ancient Greek](/wiki/Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀσκρήβιον : *Askrḗbion*, [Medieval Greek](/wiki/Medieval_Greek_language "Medieval Greek language"): Ἀσκρήβιον : Askrīvion) and was part of the [Roman province of Dalmatia](/wiki/Roman_province_of_Dalmatia "Roman province of Dalmatia").[[4]](#cite_note-Jackson2010-4)

### Middle Ages

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Middle Ages")]

The city has been fortified since the early [Middle Ages](/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), when Emperor [Justinian](/wiki/Justinian_I "Justinian I") built a fortress above Ascrivium in 535, after expelling the [Ostrogoths](/wiki/Ostrogoths "Ostrogoths").[[5]](#cite_note-5) Ascrivium was plundered by the [Saracens](/wiki/Saracens "Saracens") in 840. It was further fortified towards the peak of Saint Ivan by [Constantine VII Porphyrogennetos](/wiki/Constantine_VII "Constantine VII") in the 10th century.

It was one of the more influential [Dalmatian city-states](/wiki/Dalmatian_city-states "Dalmatian city-states"), initially with a Romance-speaking population, as throughout the early Middle Ages, and until the 11th century the [Dalmatian language](/wiki/Dalmatian_language "Dalmatian language") was still spoken in Kotor. The city was part of Byzantine Dalmatia in that period, and the modern name of Kotor probably originated in the Byzantine name for the city: *Dekatera* or *Dekaderon*.

In 1002, the city suffered damage under the occupation of the [First Bulgarian Empire](/wiki/First_Bulgarian_Empire "First Bulgarian Empire"), and in the following year it was ceded to [Duklja](/wiki/Duklja "Duklja") by the Bulgarian [Tsar Samuil](/wiki/Tsar_Samuil "Tsar Samuil"). Duklja, or Dioclea, was a vassal duchy of the Bulgarian Empire at the time. The local population resisted the pact and, taking advantage of its alliance with [Dubrovnik](/wiki/Republic_of_Ragusa "Republic of Ragusa"), maintained its high autonomy. Duklja, the biggest Serb duchy at the time, gradually became more powerful under [Vojislavljević dynasty](/wiki/Vojislavljevi%C4%87_dynasty "Vojislavljević dynasty") and eventually independent from Byzantium in 1040. The city remained autonomous up until Duklja was once again subdued by Byzantium in 1143.

The city was conquered in 1185 by [Stefan Nemanja](/wiki/Stefan_Nemanja "Stefan Nemanja"), the ruler of the [Grand Principality of Serbia](/wiki/Grand_Principality_of_Serbia "Grand Principality of Serbia") and founder of the [Nemanjić dynasty](/wiki/Nemanji%C4%87_dynasty "Nemanjić dynasty"). At that time Kotor was already an episcopal see subordinated to the archbishopric of [Bari](/wiki/Bari "Bari"), and in the 13th century, [Dominican](/wiki/Dominican_Order "Dominican Order") and [Franciscan](/wiki/Franciscan "Franciscan") monasteries were established to check the spread of [Bogomilism](/wiki/Bogomilism "Bogomilism"). Under the rule of the Nemanjić, Kotor became a partially autonomous city, enjoying many privileges and maintaining its republican institutions. This is evidenced by a statute from 1301, which demonstrates that Kotor had the status of a city under Serbian rule. In the 14th century the commerce of *Cattaro*, as named in Latin scripts (in Serbian *Котор, град краљев/Kotor, grad kraljev/Kotor, city of the King*), rivaled that of Republic of Ragusa, and caused the [Republic of Venice](/wiki/Republic_of_Venice "Republic of Venice") to be envious. Kotor remained the most important trading port of subsequent Serb states – [Kingdom of Serbia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Serbia_(medieval) "Kingdom of Serbia (medieval)") and [Serbian Empire](/wiki/Serbian_Empire "Serbian Empire"), up to its downfall in 1371.

After the [fracturing of the Serbian Empire](/wiki/Fall_of_the_Serbian_Empire "Fall of the Serbian Empire"), the city was taken by the [Kingdom of Hungary](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Hungary "Kingdom of Hungary"), only to change hands repeatedly between them and the Republic of Venice in the period between 1371 and 1384. After that, Kotor was held by the [Kingdom of Bosnia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Bosnia "Kingdom of Bosnia") under [Tvrtko I Kotromanić](/wiki/Tvrtko_I_Kotromani%C4%87 "Tvrtko I Kotromanić") between 1384 and 1391. The king of Bosnia, who claimed the Serbian throne, minted his coins in Kotor.

After the death of Tvrtko in 1391, Kotor became fully independent, until the administration, wary of the looming [Ottoman](/wiki/Ottoman_Turks "Ottoman Turks") danger, asked Venice for protection. The city acknowledged the [suzerainty](/wiki/Suzerainty "Suzerainty") of Venice in 1420.

### Venetian rule

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Venetian rule")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg/250px-Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg)](/wiki/File:Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg)

Venetian [Fortifications of Kotor](/wiki/Fortifications_of_Kotor "Fortifications of Kotor"), UNESCO site

The city was part of the [Venetian Albania](/wiki/Venetian_Albania "Venetian Albania") province of the [Venetian Republic](/wiki/Venetian_Republic "Venetian Republic") from 1420 to 1797.

Four centuries of Venetian domination have given the city the typical Venetian architecture, that contributes to make Kotor a [UNESCO](/wiki/UNESCO "UNESCO") world heritage site.[[6]](#cite_note-unesco_kotor-6)

In the 14th and 15th centuries, there was an influx of settlers from the oblasts of [Trebinje](/wiki/Trebinje "Trebinje") (the region around forts Klobuk Ledenica and Rudina) and the *[Duchy of Saint Sava](/wiki/Duchy_of_Saint_Sava "Duchy of Saint Sava")* ([Gacko](/wiki/Gacko "Gacko") and [Dabar](/wiki/Dabar_(Herzegovina) "Dabar (Herzegovina)")) to Kotor.[[7]](#cite_note-7) The Italian name of the city is *Cattaro*. Under Venetian rule, Kotor was besieged by the [Ottoman Empire](/wiki/Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") in [1538](/wiki/Ottoman%E2%80%93Venetian_War_(1537%E2%80%931540) "Ottoman–Venetian War (1537–1540)") and 1657, endured the [plague](/wiki/Plague_(disease) "Plague (disease)") in 1572, and was nearly destroyed by [earthquakes](/wiki/Earthquake "Earthquake") in 1563 and [1667](/wiki/1667_Dubrovnik_earthquake "1667 Dubrovnik earthquake").

In the 15th and 16th centuries, the customs of the local administration of Kotor, such as the right of the *popolari* to elect urban representatives, were unchanged and tolerated by the [Provveditore](/wiki/Provveditore "Provveditore") of the city, despite Venetian laws prohibiting such institutions. In 1627, during a dispute between the populari and Kotor's nobility, this right was revoked by the *consultare* [Fulgenzio Micanzio](/wiki/Fulgenzio_Micanzio "Fulgenzio Micanzio"), thus empowering the position of the city's urban elite.[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Above the entrance to the old city Kotor, is a stone relief with the [emblem of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Emblem_of_Yugoslavia "Emblem of Yugoslavia"). Following the [socialist revolution](/wiki/World_War_II_in_Yugoslavia "World War II in Yugoslavia"), it replaced a stone relief depiciting the Venetian [lion of St. Mark](/wiki/Lion_of_Saint_Mark "Lion of Saint Mark").

### Habsburg and Napoleonic rule

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Habsburg and Napoleonic rule")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg/250px-Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg)](/wiki/File:Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg)

The Cathedral Square in Cattaro depicted by [Rudolf von Alt](/wiki/Rudolf_von_Alt "Rudolf von Alt"), 1841

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/56/Napoleonov_novac_kovan_u_Kotoru_1813.png)](/wiki/File:Napoleonov_novac_kovan_u_Kotoru_1813.png)

Napoleonic coins were minted in 1813 in Kotor

After the [Treaty of Campo Formio](/wiki/Treaty_of_Campo_Formio "Treaty of Campo Formio") in 1797, it passed to the [Habsburg monarchy](/wiki/Habsburg_monarchy "Habsburg monarchy"). However, in 1805, it was assigned to the [French Empire](/wiki/First_French_Empire "First French Empire")'s client state, the [Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy_(Napoleonic) "Kingdom of Italy (Napoleonic)"), by the [Treaty of Pressburg](/wiki/Treaty_of_Pressburg_(1805) "Treaty of Pressburg (1805)"), although in fact held by a Russian squadron under [Dmitry Senyavin](/wiki/Dmitry_Senyavin "Dmitry Senyavin"). After the Russians retreated, Kotor was united in 1806 with this Kingdom of Italy and then in 1810 with the French Empire's [Illyrian Provinces](/wiki/Illyrian_Provinces "Illyrian Provinces"). Kotor was [captured by the British in an attack](/wiki/Siege_of_Cattaro "Siege of Cattaro") on the Bay led by Commodore John Harper in the brig sloop [HMS *Saracen*](/wiki/HMS_Saracen_(1812) "HMS Saracen (1812)") (18 guns). To seal off Kotor, residents along the shore literally pulled the ship in windless conditions with ropes. *Saracen'*s crew later hauled naval 18-pounder guns above Fort St. John, the fortress near Kotor, and were reinforced by Captain William Hoste with his ship [HMS *Bacchante*](/w/index.php?title=HMS_Bacchante_(1811)&action=edit&redlink=1 "HMS Bacchante (1811) (page does not exist)") (38 guns). The French garrison had no alternative but to surrender, which it did on 5 January 1814.

It was restored to the Habsburgs by the [Congress of Vienna](/wiki/Congress_of_Vienna "Congress of Vienna"). Until 1918, the town, then known as *Cattaro*, was head of the district of the same name, one of the 13 *Bezirkshauptmannschaften* in the [Kingdom of Dalmatia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Dalmatia "Kingdom of Dalmatia").[[9]](#cite_note-9)

### World War I

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: World War I")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Kotor%2C_Rathaus%2C_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg/250px-Kotor%2C_Rathaus%2C_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg)](/wiki/File:Kotor,_Rathaus,_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg)

Memorial plaque Cattaro mutiny at Kotor city hall

During [World War I](/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), Cattaro was one of three main bases of the [Austro-Hungarian Navy](/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Navy "Austro-Hungarian Navy"), the home port of the Austrian Fifth Fleet, consisting of pre-dreadnought battleships and light cruisers, and a base for Austrian and German submarines. The [Cattaro mutiny](/wiki/Cattaro_mutiny "Cattaro mutiny") of sailors of the Austro-Hungarian Navy occurred in Kotor starting on 1 February 1918. The mutiny remained isolated and had to be abandoned after three days due to the arrival of loyal troops. Four sailors were subsequently executed according to naval law.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

The area was the site of some of the fiercest battles between local Montenegrins and [Austria-Hungary](/wiki/Austria-Hungary "Austria-Hungary"). The city came under the allied [occupation of the eastern Adriatic](/wiki/Occupation_of_the_eastern_Adriatic "Occupation of the eastern Adriatic") in 1918. After 1918, the city became a part of [Yugoslavia](/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia") and officially became known as *Kotor*.

### World War II

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: World War II")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Kotor_entrance.JPG/250px-Kotor_entrance.JPG)](/wiki/File:Kotor_entrance.JPG)

Entrance of old city Kotor with post-World War II sign "What belongs to others we don't want, ours we don't give."

Between 1941 and 1943 the [Kingdom of Italy](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy") annexed the area of Kotor which became one of three provinces of the Italian [Governorate of Dalmatia](/wiki/Governorate_of_Dalmatia "Governorate of Dalmatia") – the [Province of Cattaro](/wiki/Province_of_Cattaro "Province of Cattaro")[[11]](#cite_note-11) had an area (subdivided in 15 "Comuni") of 547 km2 and a population of 39,800 inhabitants. Most of the city's inhabitants were Orthodox (with some Roman Catholics). After the war the remaining [Dalmatian Italians](/wiki/Dalmatian_Italians "Dalmatian Italians") of Kotor (300 inhabitants) left Yugoslavia towards Italy ([Istrian-Dalmatian exodus](/wiki/Istrian-Dalmatian_exodus "Istrian-Dalmatian exodus")).[[12]](#cite_note-12)

Main sights
-----------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Main sights")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/St._Tryphon%27s_Cathedral%2C_Kotor%2C_Montenegro.jpg/250px-St._Tryphon%27s_Cathedral%2C_Kotor%2C_Montenegro.jpg)](/wiki/File:St._Tryphon%27s_Cathedral,_Kotor,_Montenegro.jpg)

[St Tryphon's Cathedral](/wiki/Cathedral_of_Saint_Tryphon "Cathedral of Saint Tryphon")

Kotor has one of the best preserved medieval old towns in the Adriatic and is a double [Unesco World Heritage Site](/wiki/Unesco_World_Heritage_Site "Unesco World Heritage Site"): it is part of [Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor](/wiki/Natural_and_Culturo-Historical_Region_of_Kotor "Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor") and [Venetian Works of Defence between the 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar](/wiki/Venetian_Works_of_Defence_between_the_16th_and_17th_centuries:_Stato_da_Terra_%E2%80%93_western_Stato_da_Mar "Venetian Works of Defence between the 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar").[[6]](#cite_note-unesco_kotor-6)

It is home to numerous sights, such as the [Cathedral of Saint Tryphon](/wiki/Cathedral_of_Saint_Tryphon "Cathedral of Saint Tryphon") in the old town (built in 1166), and the ancient walls which stretch for 4.5 km (3 mi) directly above the city. Sveti Đorđe and Gospa od Škrpijela islets off the coast of [Perast](/wiki/Perast "Perast") are also among the tourism destinations in the vicinity of Kotor.

Culture
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Culture")]

Kotor hosts several summer events, such as the *Summer Carnival* or *Bokeljska Noć*. Together with [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva"), and the small town of [Tuzi](/wiki/Tuzi "Tuzi"), near [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica "Podgorica"), the city hosted the [Federation of European Carnival Cities](/wiki/Federation_of_European_Carnival_Cities "Federation of European Carnival Cities") (FECC) World Carnival City Congress in May 2009.

Kotor Festival of Theatre for Children is one of the most important festivals of its kind in Southeast Europe.[[13]](#cite_note-13) Thirty years of this manifestation have marked performances by artists from over 30 countries, from 5 continents. It was founded in 1993, not far from the place where the first play for children in the Balkans was performed in 1829. The 2017/18 festival was awarded the EFFE Label by the EFA (European Festivals Association).[[14]](#cite_note-14) Kotor Festival is highly regarded in the local community and has a large volunteer base.

Kotor has a large population of cats that have become a symbol of the city.[[15]](#cite_note-15) The city has several cat stores and a cat museum, as well as the Cats' Square (*Trg od mačaka*).[[16]](#cite_note-16) Water and food is left throughout the city for the cats to feed on, and cardboard boxes are often arranged to be a place for the cats to sleep in.[[17]](#cite_note-17) Tourists may notice cats in poor health, which may be due to malnutrition, lack of shelter, fighting, or illness (often a common viral respiratory condition for which medicine is unavailable).[[18]](#cite_note-18) The charity Kotor Kitties[[19]](#cite_note-19) exists to try and help the cats of Kotor through spaying and neutering. Kotor is described evocatively at the beginning of Marguerite Yourcenar's story 'Marko's Smile.'

Kotor is the administrative centre of Kotor municipality, which includes the towns of [Risan](/wiki/Risan "Risan") and Perast, as well as many small hamlets around the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor"), and has a population of 21,916.[[21]](#cite_note-Monstat-21)

The town of Kotor itself has 1,360 inhabitants, but the administrative limits of the town encompass only the area of the Old Town. The urban area of Kotor also includes [Dobrota](/wiki/Dobrota "Dobrota") (7,345) and [Škaljari](/wiki/%C5%A0kaljari "Škaljari") (3,342), bringing the population of Kotor's urban area close to 13,000 inhabitants. The total number rises to around 15,000 if the neighbouring hamlets of [Muo](/wiki/Muo "Muo"), [Prčanj](/wiki/Pr%C4%8Danj "Prčanj") and [Stoliv](/w/index.php?title=Stoliv&action=edit&redlink=1 "Stoliv (page does not exist)") are included. The entire population of [Kotor Municipality](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality") was 21,916, as of the 2023 census.

Throughout history, there was a significant [Italian-speaking community](/wiki/Dalmatian_Italians "Dalmatian Italians") in Kotor. Until the 19th century the main language of Kotor was [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"),[[23]](#cite_note-23) which then began to decline in favour of [Serbian](/wiki/Serbian_language "Serbian language"). According to the Austrian censuses, there were 623 residents of the central settlement that used [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language") as their *habitual language*[[24]](#cite_note-Seton-24) (18.7% of the total population) in 1890, and 257 (8.1%) in 1910.[[25]](#cite_note-:02-25) The commune as a whole had 646 (11.9%) Italian speakers in 1890, and 274 (4.6%) in 1910.[[25]](#cite_note-:02-25) The majority of the Italian population left the city for Italy after the [Treaty of Rapallo (1920)](/wiki/Treaty_of_Rapallo_(1920) "Treaty of Rapallo (1920)").[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] In 2011, only 31 people declared themselves as Italians, corresponding to 0.14% of the total population.[[26]](#cite_note-26)

In 1848, the population of the city of Kotor itself was 3,550 people, of whom 2,384 were [Catholics](/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") and 1,157 were [Orthodox Christians](/wiki/Serbian_Orthodox_Church "Serbian Orthodox Church"). However, the *Circolo* (administrative area) of which Kotor was the capital had a population of 34,326, of whom the majority (24,498) were Orthodox and a minority (9,819) were Catholic.[[27]](#cite_note-27) The population of the city proper increased to 5,400 by 1890 and 5,700 by 1900.[[28]](#cite_note-28)

According to documents from 1900, Kotor had 7,617 Catholics, and 7,207 Orthodox Christians. Kotor is still the seat of the [Catholic](/wiki/Catholic "Catholic") [Bishopric of Kotor](/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Kotor "Roman Catholic Diocese of Kotor"), which covers the entire gulf. In 2011, 78% citizens of Kotor were Orthodox Christians, while 12% were listed as Roman Catholic.

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Sports")]

The local football team is [FK Bokelj](/wiki/FK_Bokelj "FK Bokelj"), who have spent several seasons in the country's [top](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League") and [second tiers](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League"). They play their home games at the [Stadion pod Vrmcem](/wiki/Stadion_pod_Vrmcem "Stadion pod Vrmcem").

Kotor is a national powerhouse of [water polo](/wiki/Water_polo "Water polo"), which is a popular sport in Montenegro. The team of [Primorac Kotor](/wiki/Primorac_Kotor "Primorac Kotor") won the [LEN Champions League](/wiki/LEN_Champions_League "LEN Champions League") in 2009. Another club from Kotor, [VA Cattaro](/wiki/VA_Cattaro "VA Cattaro"), won the 2010 edition of the [LEN Euro Cup](/wiki/LEN_Euro_Cup "LEN Euro Cup").

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Transport")]

Kotor is connected to the [Adriatic Highway](/wiki/Adriatic_Highway "Adriatic Highway") and the rest of the coast and inland Montenegro by [Vrmac Tunnel](/wiki/Vrmac_Tunnel "Vrmac Tunnel"). Inland is reachable by detouring from Adriatic highway at Budva or [Sutomore](/wiki/Sutomore "Sutomore") (through [Sozina tunnel](/wiki/Sozina_tunnel "Sozina tunnel")). There is also a historic road connecting Kotor with [Cetinje](/wiki/Cetinje "Cetinje"), which has views of Kotor bay.

[Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade"), [Moscow](/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), [Paris](/wiki/Paris "Paris") and [London](/wiki/London "London"). Dozens of charter planes land daily on Tivat airport during the summer season.

[Podgorica Airport](/wiki/Podgorica_Airport "Podgorica Airport") is 65 kilometres (40 mi) away, and it has regular flights to major European destinations throughout the year.

Tourism
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Kotor&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Tourism")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg/250px-Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg)](/wiki/File:Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg)

Cruise Ships Arrive at Kotor in June 2024

Kotor is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Montenegro due to its well-preserved medieval architecture.[[30]](#cite_note-30) In 2019, it welcomed over 250,000 tourists.[[31]](#cite_note-31)

In June 2021, the first and only public aquarium in Montenegro, [Aquarium Boka](/wiki/Aquarium_Boka "Aquarium Boka"), was opened in Kotor.[[32]](#cite_note-:0-32) It is the organizational unit of the [Institute for Marine Biology](/w/index.php?title=Institute_for_Marine_Biology_of_the_University_of_Montenegro&action=edit&redlink=1 "Institute for Marine Biology of the University of Montenegro (page does not exist)") of the [University of Montenegro](/wiki/University_of_Montenegro "University of Montenegro"), a unique institution in Montenegro that combines research and education to promote and practice the efficient conservation of marine wildlife.[[33]](#cite_note-:1-33) In the first three months, the Aquarium was visited by more than 8,000 people.[[34]](#cite_note-34)
